VOLUME 9 (PART 4): THE TEN DEMONIC STATES OF THE FEELING SKANDHA

Brief Commentary on the Shurangama Sutra — Venerable Master Hsuan Hua

THE SHURANGAMA SUTRA

THE FIFTY SKANDHA-DEMONS

Lectured by Venerable Master Hsuan Hua at

The Buddhist Lecture Hall, San Francisco

California _ USA _ 1968

THE FEELING SKANDHA

THE MENTAL STATE BEFORE ENTERING THE FEELING SKANDHA

Sutra text: A-nan, bỉ thiện nam tử, tu tam-ma-đề, xa ma tha trung, sắc âm tận giả, kiến chư Phật tâm, như minh kính trung, hiển hiện kì tượng.

Translation: Ananda, that good man cultivating samadhi, within shamatha, with the form skandha exhausted, sees the Buddhas' minds as images appearing in a bright mirror.

Commentary: Ananda, that good man cultivating samadhi.

Cultivating the effort of “returning the hearing to hear the self-nature,” turning the hearing inward to recognize one's own nature – cultivating samadhi means cultivating right concentration: cultivating the perfect penetration of the ear organ, the effort of “returning the hearing to hear the self-nature,” turning the hearing inward to recognize one's own nature – the effort for attaining perfect, penetrating wisdom through the ear organ. When cultivating the shamatha Dharma, purifying the mind, transforming all false thoughts to focus on contemplation – when the form skandha is utterly exhausted, one can see the Buddhas' mind-seal Dharma as if seeing oneself in a mirror.

What happens when you dissolve the entire form skandha? You can see the Buddhas' mind-seal Dharma as if seeing yourself in a mirror.

THE SCOPE OF THE FEELING SKANDHA

Sutra text: Nhược hữu sở đắc, nhi vị năng dụng. Do như yểm nhân, thủ túc uyển nhiên kiến văn bất hoặc, tâm xúc khách tà, nhi bất năng động. Thử tắc danh vi thọ ấm khu vũ.

Translation: As if having gained something, yet unable to use it – like a person pressed by a nightmare-demon: limbs intact, seeing and hearing undeluded, yet the mind afflicted by an intruding evil, unable to move. This is called the region of the feeling skandha.

Commentary: As if having gained something, yet unable to use it. Like a person pressed by a nightmare-demon.

I spoke before of the kumbhanda ghosts – a kind of nightmare ghosts that often use mantras to spell people sick to death. When a person is possessed by such a ghost, the limbs remain intact, not lost; seeing and hearing are undeluded and unconfused, yet the mind is controlled by the flock of evils to the point of being unable to move. This is called the region of the feeling skandha.

THE ROOT OF THE FEELING SKANDHA

Sutra text: Nhược yểm cữu yết, kì tâm li thân, phản quán kì diện, khứ trụ tự do, vô phục lưu ngại. Danh thọ ấm  tận. Thị nhân tắc năng siêu việt kiến trược. Quán kì sở do, hư minh vọng tưởng, dĩ vi kì bản.

Translation: When the nightmare lifts, the mind leaves the body, looks back upon one's own face, going and staying at will, with no more obstruction. This is called the exhaustion of the feeling skandha. Such a person can then transcend the defilement of views. Contemplate its cause: empty, bright false thought is its root.

Commentary: When the paralysis of the nightmare eases and the mind leaves the body, looking back upon one's own face.

While still within the region of the feeling skandha, it is like being paralyzed by a kumbhanda ghost, so you cannot be at ease. If this condition vanishes and the feeling skandha is wholly removed, the mind escapes the body and you can see your own face, going and staying at will – going or not going as you wish, entirely unbound, unobstructed. This is called the exhaustion of the feeling skandha.

When the feeling skandha has dissolved, such a person can transcend the defilement of views – one of the five turbidities of the evil age.

Contemplate its cause: empty, bright false thought is the root of the feeling skandha. When the feeling skandha is utterly destroyed, its root vanishes as well.

THE 10 STATES OF THE FEELING SKANDHA

* * *

1 – EXCESSIVE COMPASSION (THE DEMON OF COMPASSION)

Sutra text: A-nan bỉ thiện nam tử, đương  tại thử trung, đắc đại quang diệu, kỳ tâm phát minh, nội ức quá phần. Hốt ư kì xứ, phát vô cùng bi, như thị nãi chí, quán  kiến văn manh, do như xích tử , tâm sinh lân mẫn, bất giác lưu lệ.

Translation: Ananda, that good man, right within this state, gaining great bright light, his mind enlightened, inwardly suppressing excessively – suddenly, right there, gives rise to boundless compassion, to the point of seeing mosquitoes and gnats as newborn babes, his heart filling with pity, weeping unawares.

Commentary: Ananda, that good man, right within this state, his mind very bright, inwardly suppressing excessively. A kind of emotion suddenly arises: he has continuously restrained thought to excess, and with inner repression overdone, suddenly gives rise to boundless compassion and fondness for all beings, to the point of seeing mosquitoes and gnats as newborn babes – newborn babe in Chinese is chi zi, because a newborn's skin is red.

His heart filling with pity, weeping unawares – not knowing why he bursts into tears.

Sutra text: Thử danh công dụng  ức tồi quá việt. Ngộ tắc vô cữu, phi vi thánh chứng. Giác liễu bất mê, cửu tự tiêu yết. Nhược tác thánh giải, tắc hữu bi ma  nhập kì tâm phủ, kiến nhân tắc bi  đề khấp vô hạn. Thất ư chánh thọ, đương tòng luân trụy.

Translation: This is called excessive repression of the mind in the course of effort. Recognized, it is without fault – not sage realization. Awakened and undeluded, in time it vanishes of itself. But if interpreted as sagehood, a demon of compassion enters the very heart, and on seeing people one pities them, weeping without restraint. Losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

Commentary: This is called excessive repression of the mind in the course of effort.

This state can arise during effort in cultivation – it occurs because you have repressed the mind excessively. Recognized, it is without fault, not sage realization. If awakened and undeluded, in time it vanishes of itself – if you realize you have erred and silently ask yourself why you weep so groundlessly, then change at once. Realizing this, the tension will no longer remain.

This state is not sage realization – it does not mean you have realized the mind of same-substance great compassion. Do not think that pitying mosquitoes, gnats, and tiny insects as your own newborn babes is the mind of same-substance great compassion.

If awakened thus, no longer deluded, that tense state vanishes of itself. But if you think you have realized sagehood – if you think: “Oh! Now I have the mind of same-substance great compassion – my cultivation effort has truly succeeded” – then a demon of compassion enters the very heart: meeting anyone at all, you burst into tears for no reason. This demon on seeing people pities them, weeping without restraint, weeping without knowing why it is so sorrowful.

When I was in Manchuria, I knew a woman named Liu Jin-tong who met with such a state: whenever meeting anyone, she would burst into tears and say: “In a past life you were my child. Now the child has returned – found its mother.” With tears she thoroughly perplexed people, making them believe they had truly met their mother. In fact that person had met a demon. (8)

Losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall: if you obey the demon kings, you will fall into the hells.

2 – EXCESSIVE ZEAL

Sutra text: A-nan, hựu bỉ định trung, chư thiện nam tử, kiến sắc ấm tiêu, thọ ấm  minh bạch, thắng tướng hiện tiền, cảm kích quá phần. Hốt ư kì trung, sanh vô hạn dũng, kỳ tâm mãnh lợi, chí tề chư Phật. Vị tam tăng kì, nhất niệm năng việt.

Translation: Further, Ananda, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve and the feeling skandha clearly revealed, a surpassing appearance manifests and they are stirred to excess. Suddenly within it arises boundless valor: the mind keen and sharp, aspiring to equal the Buddhas, claiming to transcend three asamkhyeya eons in a single thought.

Commentary: Further, Ananda, when good men – including all good people cultivating the Buddhadharma – in this samadhi-state, see the form skandha dissolved and the feeling skandha clearly revealed: among the five aggregates, clearly knowing the form skandha has dissolved and fully, brightly knowing the feeling skandha.

Then a surpassing appearance manifests – a special, rare vision appears in the mind.

The cultivator feels very buoyant and at ease. Yet excess is as bad as deficiency: there is little difference between going too far and falling short of the goal – neither accords with the Middle Way. As when traveling: overshooting your destination is the same as not arriving. So in this samadhi-state one is stirred to excess, then suddenly gives rise to a valorous resolve, keen and sharp, aspiring to equal the Buddhas –

valorously vigorous as never before, deeming oneself equal to the Buddhas, saying the Buddha and oneself are the same – claiming to transcend the three asamkhyeya eons in a single thought.

Claiming to transcend the first, second, and third asamkhyeya eons in a single thought – hence declaring oneself a Buddha. Not only calling oneself a Buddha, but calling everyone Buddhas. Such a person has fallen into wrong knowledge and wrong views.

In fact, everyone has a Buddha in mind, but cultivation effort is needed to recognize the Buddha-nature. Even with determined cultivation, one cannot become a Buddha in a single thought – a very long time is required. Though that time may be shortened through understanding and practicing the right Dharma, becoming a Buddha in a single thought is still hardly possible. One who cultivates without a good spiritual friend's guidance, however bitterly he practices, will only grow wrong views throughout his cultivation: seeing that after such long cultivation it amounts to becoming a Buddha anyway, he decides he is a Buddha – elevating himself to equality with the Buddhas. This situation occurs as the feeling skandha dissolves: he says he is equal to the Buddhas. Indeed, with that single mistaken thought he joins Mara's retinue.

Sutra text: Thử danh công dụng, lăng suất quá việt. Ngộ tắc vô cữu, phi vi thánh chứng. Giác liễu bất mê, cửu tự tiêu yết. Nhược tác thánh giải, tắc hữu cuồng ma, nhập kì tâm phủ, kiến nhân tắc khoa, ngã mạn vô tỉ. Kỳ tâm nãi chí, thượng bất kiến Phật, hạ bất kiến nhân. Thất ư chánh thọ, đương tòng luân trụy.

Translation: This is called over-exceeding vigor in effort. Recognized, it is without fault – not sage realization. If awakened and undeluded, in time it vanishes of itself. But if interpreted as sagehood, a demon of madness enters the very heart, and on meeting people one boasts of oneself, incomparably arrogant – the mind to the point of above seeing no Buddhas, below seeing no people. Losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

Commentary: Now you are hearing the Shurangama Sutra lectured: we have reached the very important chapter on the fifty demonic phenomena arising from the five skandhas. If cultivators do not understand these Fifty Skandha-Demon Phenomena, they will easily go astray in their effort. If you recognize these skandha-demon phenomena, you will not lose self-mastery and recklessly boast, pretending to be someone important. So I urge you to encourage your relatives and friends to come hear this section on the Fifty Skandha-Demon Phenomena lectured – it will help you know each kind of state in cultivation.

This is called over-exceeding vigor in effort. This state occurs as a result of the cultivator's effort in practice: the consequence of excessive effort transforming the inner self-nature makes him so valorous. There is nothing wrong in being valorous and vigorous if you use it to advance your cultivation of the right Dharma. But you should not proudly say: “Oh! I am a Buddha!” Are you a Buddha? The Buddha taught the Tripitaka and the twelve divisions of sutras – how many divisions, how many pitakas have you spoken? You do not even understand the sutra pitaka – what talk of your being a Buddha? Is that not absurd? The Buddha spoke the entire sutra pitaka, while you have never spoken a single sutra or pitaka – how dare you proclaim you have become a Buddha? Even if you could master every principle and clearly lecture the Tripitaka and twelve divisions, at most you could call yourself a disciple of the Buddha, not a Buddha. But this person feels everyone in the world reveres and treasures the Buddha, so he wishes to become like the Buddha himself, so that after death people will make offerings. In fact after death he will be buried deep in the earth, turned to dust – nothing remaining with him at all.

Recognized, it is without fault – not sage realization.

It is perfectly fine to have such valorous vigor, so long as you understand: it is only a state, and does not mean you have realized the sage fruition. That state is not sage realization. If awakened thus and maintaining clarity, in time that state vanishes of itself.

But if you deem yourself to have realized sagehood – saying: Oh! I have become a Buddha – a demon of madness at once enters the very heart.

So you see: if you still do not clearly understand the Fifty Skandha-Demon Phenomena, how could you become a Buddha? This demon is one of the mad, arrogant, egotistic kinds: it slips into your mind, possessing you as its property, governing the possessed person's mind and nature – once possessed, the demon king controls and acts as that person.

Meeting anyone at all, one boasts of oneself – deeming oneself right and everyone else wrong, disparaging and smearing others while praising oneself. Everyone is entirely wrong; only it alone is worthy. It thinks it has become a Buddha.

One becomes incomparably arrogant toward everyone; the mind to the point of above seeing no Buddhas, below seeing no people. Why? Because it thinks it is itself a Buddha – and sees no one below itself anymore.

What then does it see? It says everyone is a Buddha; it itself is also a Buddha. There is no Buddha above it anymore – nor will there ever be a Buddha surpassing it. That is the state of seeing no one below itself anymore.

Losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

Without maintaining right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

3 – EXCESSIVE DEJECTION (THE DEMON OF HEAVY RECOLLECTION)

Sutra text: Hựu bỉ định trung, chư thiện nam tử, kiến sắc ấm tiêu, thọ ấm  minh bạch. Tiền vô tân chứng, quy thất cố cư. Trí lực  suy vi, nhập trung đọa địa, quýnh vô sở kiến. Tâm trung hốt nhiên, sanh đại khô kiệt. Ư nhất thiết thời, trầm ức bất tán. Tương thử dĩ vi cần tinh tiến tướng.

Translation: Further, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve and the feeling skandha clearly revealed – ahead no new realization to attain, behind the old dwelling lost – wisdom-power weakening, entering a doomed place with nothing in view – suddenly the mind gives rise to great aridity. At all times sunk in recollection, unrelieved – mistaking this for the mark of diligence and vigor.

Commentary: Further, when good men in this samadhi-state see the form skandha dissolved and the feeling skandha clearly revealed – ahead no new state to realize, behind the formerly realized state lost – wisdom-power weakening. No new state to realize ahead; retreating, the formerly self-realized state is lost – hence wisdom-power wanes.

Advancing, there is nothing to attain; behind the cultivator, the state long dwelt in has vanished. Wisdom now grows weak; the cultivator is no longer valorous and keen as at first. This is the case of suddenly progressing, then abruptly halting. Fallen into a doomed place – where the cultivator nearly falls – seeing nothing in view: the cultivator feels or senses nothing anymore.

Suddenly the mind gives rise to great aridity.

The cultivator's feeling now is of utter monotony, dryness, craving: everything seems meaningless and tiresome; craving, because he needs to be moistened by the waters of the Buddhadharma. He feels parched and withered, seeing nothing more. This state resembles a beginner unwilling to cultivate, constantly feeling lonely and dejected – and that loneliness and dejection surely lead to affliction, the inherent affliction.

I had not planned to raise this point, but I fear some may not understand. Moreover: it is like a woman longing for a man, yearning until she feels restless and uneasy; likewise when a man yearns for a woman, he feels the same unease. Both are lonely and dreary, as if having lost something never to be found again.

At all times the cultivator is sunk in recollection, unrelieved.

Like a man and woman lovesick for each other, yearning for each other, never forgetting.

Mistaking this for the mark of diligence and vigor.

This state grips thought so tightly it will not disperse, making him mistake it for a kind of vigor in effort.

Sutra text: Thử danh tu tâm, vô huệ tự thất, ngộ tắc vô cữu, phi vi thánh chứng. Nhược tác thánh giải, tắc hữu ức ma, nhập kì tâm phủ. Đán tịch toát tâm, huyền tại nhất xứ. Thất ư chánh thọ đương tòng  luân trụy.

Translation: This is called cultivating the mind without wisdom, bringing loss upon oneself. Recognized, it is without fault – not sage realization. But if interpreted as sagehood, a demon of recollection enters the very heart: day and night holding the mind suspended in one place. Losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

Commentary: This is called cultivating the mind without wisdom, bringing loss upon oneself. Within the scope of the feeling skandha, this is called cultivating without wisdom, bringing error upon oneself.

You have not yet developed wisdom – but do not fret for not having developed wisdom. Recognized, it is without fault: if you understand it is only a state, nothing is amiss. But if you do not understand, you will always get caught in “clinging to emptiness” and stagnate in stillness. If you always scatter the mind in fancies, you will sink and never accomplish the Way.

This state is not sage realization – it does not mean you have just realized something or may call yourself a sage. Do not mistake a thief for your son.

But if you deem yourself awakened, a demon of recollection will enter the heart.

Do you hear? This is truly dangerous. If you regard it as a wholesome state, a kind of recollection-demon will come to help you remember everything well. And if you cannot remember something? It will help you remember. Knowing how much you wish to remember, it enters your mind to help you remember – to that extent.

Day and night holding the mind suspended in one place.

Your mind will be drawn and held to a single point.

Losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

Lacking right samadhi (not easily attaining right samadhi), one is sure to fall – in the future falling into the hells.

4 – SELF-SATISFACTION (TAKING A LITTLE FOR ENOUGH)

Sutra text: Hựu bỉ định trung, chư thiện nam tử, kiến sắc ấm tiêu, thọ ấm  minh bạch. Huệ lực quá định, thất ư mãnh lợi. Dĩ chư thắng tánh, hoài ư tâm trung. Tự tâm dĩ nghi, thị Lô-giá-na, đắc thiểu vi túc.

Translation: Further, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve and the feeling skandha clearly revealed – wisdom-power exceeding samadhi, erring in keen sharpness – embracing a surpassing nature within the heart, deeming one's own mind to be Vairocana, taking a little attainment for enough.

Commentary: Further, when good men in this samadhi-state see the form skandha dissolved and the feeling skandha clearly revealed.

Wisdom-power exceeding samadhi. The power of wisdom surpasses the power of samadhi.

Erring in keen sharpness – mistaken through sharp, keen wisdom, passing through a reckless, hasty feeling – fond of embracing a surpassing nature of one's own within the heart. Deeming one's own mind to be Vairocana – imagining oneself to be Vairocana Buddha.

In this state the cultivator regards his own nature as surpassing and constantly dwells on it – cherishing fancies of a surpassing nature, mistaking himself for Vairocana Buddha.

Vairocana – the Sanskrit root meaning “light shining everywhere.” The cultivator must not imagine he is already Vairocana Buddha.

Taking a little attainment for enough. Content with one's paltry attainment.

The cultivator gains a little progress and grows content – yet that samadhi power is vastly different from the Buddha's great samadhi power – while he proclaims himself to have become Vairocana Buddha.

Sutra text: Thử danh dụng tâm, vong thất hằng thẩm, nịch ư tri kiến. Ngộ tắc vô cữu, phi vi thánh chứng. Nhược tác thánh giải, tắc hữu hạ liệt, di tri túc ma, nhập kì tâm phủ. Kiến nhân tự ngôn, ngã đắc vô thượng đệ nhất nghĩa đế. Thất ư chánh thọ, đương tòng luân trụy.

Translation: This is called applying the mind while forgetting constant self-examination, drowning in views and knowledge. Recognized, it is without fault – not sage realization. But if interpreted as sagehood, a base demon of easily-contented transformation enters the very heart, and on meeting people claims: I have attained the unsurpassed foremost truth. Losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

Commentary: This state is called “applying the mind while forgetting constant self-examination, drowning in views and knowledge.” You do not constantly apply effort in examining yourself, becoming stagnant in views and knowledge – unable to distinguish what you know and think, you stagnate, stuck in your own private ideas and notions.

Recognized, it is without fault – nothing will go wrong.

That state is not sage realization. But if interpreted as sagehood – thinking you have realized some surpassing state – then a base demon – the basest, most depraved and disgusting kind of demon – of easily-contented transformation enters the very heart: content in any circumstance, entering your very heart – the demon clings to your mind, possessing your mind as its property, driving your spirit out of your body. All that remains is a deluded shell of a body, yet you do not realize it.

On meeting people at once claiming: I have attained the unsurpassed foremost truth. There is now a man who often stands on Grand Avenue in San Francisco's Chinatown shopping district, dressed in gaudy clothes of many colors, telling passersby:

“I cultivated in the mountains and forests for five years and am now awakened; now I have such-and-such spiritual powers…”

He formerly bowed to me as teacher and became my disciple, but he did not follow what I taught. Before I came to America, can you guess what he did? With a gourd bearing a painted stripe slung over his shoulder, he proclaimed himself my disciple, claiming to have learned great skill from me; further claiming he could answer any question anyone asked. He used my name to cheat people. Now that I have come to America, he still cheats people – though he no longer uses my name to deceive. This is precisely the kind of demon this sutra passage addresses: he claims to have attained the foremost truth.

Losing all right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

He has lost all right samadhi, no longer following what I taught. Since I came here, he never comes to hear sutra lectures or Dharma talks – only proclaiming he has attained the Way, is awakened, has spiritual powers. What powers does he actually have? You would never guess! They are money, money, money. So he is sure to fall.

5 – ANXIETY AND GLOOM (THE DEMON OF PERIL)

Sutra text: Hựu bỉ định trung, chư thiện nam tử, kiến sắc ấm tiêu, thọ ấm  minh bạch. Tân chứng vị hoạch, cố tâm dĩ vong. Lịch lãm nhị tế, tự sanh gian hiểm. Ư tâm hốt nhiên, sanh vô tận  ưu, như tọa thiết sàng, như ẩm độc dược. Tâm bất dục hoạt, thường cầu ư nhân, linh hại kì mạng, tảo thú giải thoát.

Translation: Further, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve and the feeling skandha clearly revealed – the new realization not yet gained, the former mind already lost – examining both ends, they find themselves in peril. Suddenly the mind gives rise to boundless sorrow, as if seated on an iron bed, as if drinking poison. Not wishing to live, they constantly ask others to harm their lives, that liberation come soon.

Commentary: Further, when good men are in this samadhi.

Now the cultivator has a somewhat deeper samadhi power. Seeing the form skandha dissolved and the feeling skandha clearly revealed – the new realization not yet gained, the former mind already lost. The cultivator sees nothing more to realize; the formerly realized mind-state has vanished. Examining both ends, they find themselves in peril. Closely examining the two shores of past and future, seeing both gone, one feels as if meeting great peril.

He thinks: “Oh no! This is truly perilous! Terrible!”

Suddenly the mind gives rise to boundless sorrow: his heart fills with grief and affliction over everything – and grief itself brings affliction. Affliction how? As if seated on an iron bed: from morning to night he thinks:

“Oh, I am as if seated on an iron bed in the hells. What shall I do now? Having this body is truly suffering.”

As if drinking poison, feeling about to die. Not wishing to live.

All day he thinks: better for me to die.

In China there is a saying: “Better to die – it saves clothes.”

This person has perhaps thought so, saying: “Better to die! Better to die!”

In most cases of suicide, demons are involved: the demon bows to the victim and recites a mantra. But the victim cannot hear what mantra the demon recites. The meaning of the mantra demons usually recite is: “Better for you to die, better for you to die! Hurry – the sooner life ends, the better!”

Because the victim is so focused on suicide, he cannot hear it with his ears, yet through the subconscious the demon's mantra seizes the whole soul. Since demons have the power of knowing others' minds, they can let demonic power seep into the victim's mind, inciting suicide. The victim's mind obeys the demon's temptation and believes what the demon says: so they drink poison, hang themselves, drown themselves in the sea, or leap from the Golden Gate Bridge into the river. That is how victims kill themselves. There are a great many demons around the Golden Gate Bridge. They dare not trouble you if you are full of yang energy. But if someone passes there with weak yang energy – essence, energy, and spirit all weak – the demons say: “Better for you to die, better for you to die!…” and the person leaps into the river. Most suicides are incited by demons.

Constantly asking others to destroy their own lives, that liberation come soon.

He constantly tells others: Please kill me! If you have any way to help me end my life, that would be wonderful – I shall be liberated.

Sutra text: Thử danh tu hành, thất ư phương tiện. Ngộ tắc vô cữu, phi vi thánh chứng. Nhược tác thánh giải, tắc hữu nhất phần, thường ưu sầu ma, nhập kì tâm phủ. Thủ chấp đao kiếm tự cát kì nhục, hân kì xả thọ, hoặc thường ưu sầu, tẩu nhập sơn lâm, bất nại kiến nhân. Thất ư chánh thọ, đương tòng luân trụy.

Translation: This is called cultivating while losing skillful means. Recognized, it is without fault – not sage realization. But if interpreted as sagehood, a kind of ever-sorrowful demon enters the very heart: grasping knives and swords, slashing one's own flesh, delighting in casting life away; or ever sorrowful, fleeing into forests and mountains, unable to bear seeing people. Losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

Commentary: This is called cultivating while losing skillful means.

Because the cultivator does not clearly understand expedient Dharma-doors, this mistaken attachment arises. Once the attachment has arisen, if the cultivator recognizes it, it is without fault – nothing is amiss – not sage realization: this does not mean he has realized sagehood. Now that you have heard the principles from this Sutra, you must be extremely cautious – do not let the mind drift freely in false thoughts. Do not give rise to thoughts of wanting to die, or to the thought that you cannot attain what you wish. If you keep such thoughts, you will attract this kind of demon at once – in this world they are very many. So you should not let your mind drift in false thoughts or speak carelessly and casually. If you do, this kind of demon will possess you at once; when that happens, you will be unable to bear it – losing freedom, even if you do not wish to die, there will be no way to avoid death.

But if you think you have realized sagehood, a kind of ever-sorrowful demon will come. You think you are sad and dejected – and that dejected sorrow also involves a kind of demon. Why are you disappointed or angry? If you opened your own Buddha eye, you would see: if people do not get angry, there are no demons at all – but the moment people get angry, demons taunt: “Flare up! Rage! Make havoc!”

Behind the scenes it urges you to flare up. Whether or not you believe me, what I say is still the truth – and if you do not believe my words, there is only the waste of time. Try it and see!

Entering the very heart – possessing your body – grasping knives and swords, slashing one's own flesh.

Have I not told you about Filial Son Wang? He is Master Chang Ren, who practiced filial conduct beside his parents' graves. One day, in samadhi, he saw bandits seizing his nephew and about to shoot him some five miles from where Master Chang Ren was – but just as a bandit was about to pull the trigger, from within samadhi Master Chang Ren brushed the gun aside with his hand so the bullet missed, and the nephew escaped. Behind this event, a ghost wanted to take the nephew's life – it had made the bandits come seize and try to kill the nephew.

Such are karmic connections: the ghost sought to kill the nephew, but Master Chang Ren blocked it, so the ghost could only stand behind him, unable to do anything to him – then it went to his younger brother, Second Master Wang, possessing him in place of the elder. Second Master Wang, knife in hand, went to the graves seeking Master Chang Ren, intending to kill himself before him.

The ghost wanted to kill the younger brother, yet strangely, knife raised ready to strike his own head, the ghost could not bring its murderous hand down. Meanwhile Master Chang Ren was reciting the Diamond Sutra; and while he recited, my own teacher (Master Chang Zhi), then not yet left home, felt uneasy within, as if something terrible were happening – worried and restless, wondering whether something had happened to Filial Son Wang out at the graves. He hurried to the cemetery to see – and indeed saw Second Master Wang holding a knife about to stab himself.

Filial Son Wang (Master Chang Ren) had written a few words beforehand for my teacher (Master Chang Zhi): “Go buy some paper spirit-money (by Chinese custom, people burn paper money as offerings for the dead). I shall recite the Diamond Sutra praying for this ghost's deliverance. There is a ghost involved in this matter – such is my vow.” After Filial Son Wang recited the sutra for the ghost's deliverance, nothing more happened.

However, this is only an example of the kind of demon under discussion – but in this case the ghost came wanting to take a life, not because of cultivation effort: for Filial Son Wang, while cultivating, still cared about the affairs of his kin. He blocked this ghost's attempt to kill his younger brother; the ghost could not kill Filial Son Wang because he had samadhi power and gave rise to no false thoughts, so the ghost could do nothing to him and went to harm the younger brother instead.

Delighting in casting life away – delighting in dying.

Or ever sorrowful: now that you have heard this sutra passage lectured, be careful not to grieve all day long anymore; do not constantly complain and feel afflicted. If you keep feeling sad and disappointed, this kind of demon will come possess your body at once. This happens partly through the demon's power and partly through your own mind: the demon borrows your spirit to act. If your mind abides in right views, nothing will go wrong; but if your thinking is not upright, the demon will command you – if it tells you to grieve, you grieve, until you flee into deep hiding, shunning everyone.

Fleeing into forests and mountains, unable to bear seeing people. Losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

Such a person is sure to fall into the hells in the future.

6̉ – BOUNDLESS JOY (THE DEMON OF JOY)

Sutra text: Hựu bỉ định trung, chư thiện nam tử, kiến sắc ấm tiêu, thọ ấm  minh bạch. Xử thanh tịnh trung, tâm an ổn hậu. Hốt nhiên tự hữu, vô hạn hỉ sanh. Tâm trung hoan duyệt, bất năng tự chỉ .

Translation: Further, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve and the feeling skandha clearly revealed – dwelling within purity, the mind secure and stable – suddenly, of itself, boundless joy arises; the heart rejoicing, unable to restrain itself.

Commentary: Further, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve and the feeling skandha clearly revealed. Again, when the cultivator in samadhi sees the form skandha dissolved and clearly recognizes the feeling skandha – dwelling within the purity of right samadhi, the mind secure and stable: the mind utterly calm and steady, without a trace of distraction or false thought. Right at that point, the feeling skandha gives rise to another function.

Suddenly boundless joy arises in the mind – feeling joy welling up, knowing that joy boundless, its measure immeasurable. The heart rejoicing, unable to restrain itself – unable to stop itself: even wishing to end that merriment, one cannot.

Sutra text: Thử danh khinh an, vô huệ tự  cấm. Ngộ tắc vô cữu, phi vi thánh chứng.

Translation: This is called the mind at ease, but lacking the wisdom to restrain itself. Recognized, it is without fault – not sage realization.

Commentary: This is called the mind at ease, but lacking the wisdom to restrain that joyful state – the cultivator lacks the wisdom to control this joyful feeling.

Recognized, it is without fault – not sage realization.

This does not mean you have become a sage.

Sutra text: Nhược tác thánh giải, tắc hữu nhất phần, hảo hỉ lạc ma nhập kì tâm phủ, kiến nhân tắc tiếu, ư cù lộ bàng, tự ca tự vũ. Tự vị dĩ đắc, vô ngại giải thoát. Thất ư chánh thọ, đương tòng luân trụy.

Translation: But if interpreted as sagehood, a kind of joy-loving demon enters the very heart, and on meeting people one laughs, singing and dancing by the roadside. Claiming to have attained unobstructed liberation – losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

Commentary: But if you deem yourself to have realized sagehood.

If you say: “Oh! Now I have entered the Ground of Joy – I am a Bodhisattva of the Ground of Joy!” – then a joy-loving demon enters your mind. On meeting people at once laughing, singing and dancing by the roadside – like a hippie who has entirely lost self-control: waving both arms, stamping both feet, singing and dancing all kinds of music.

Claiming to have attained unobstructed liberation. Losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

Losing all right samadhi, right views, and all power of reason – in the end falling into the hells.

7 – GREAT ARROGANCE (THE DEMON OF ARROGANCE)

Sutra text: Hựu bỉ định trung, chư thiện nam tử, kiến sắc ấm tiêu, thọ ấm minh bạch, tự vị dĩ túc. Hốt hữu vô đoan, đại ngã mạn khởi, như thị nãi chí, mạn dữ quá mạn, cập mạn quá mạn, hoặc tăng thượng mạn, hoặc ti liệt mạn, nhất thời câu phát. Tâm trung thượng khinh, thập phương Như Lai, hà huống hạ vị, Thanh văn Duyên giác.

Translation: Further, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve and the feeling skandha clearly revealed, deeming themselves already complete – suddenly, for no reason, great arrogance arises: thus pride, exceeding pride, pride exceeding the excellent, superiority pride, and inferiority pride all arise at once. In the mind even slighting the Tathagatas of the ten directions – how much more the lower ranks of Hearers and Pratyekabuddhas.

Commentary: Further, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve and the feeling skandha clearly revealed, deeming themselves already complete.

Seeing oneself as having everything in full – having realized fruitions, awakened, become a Buddha.

Suddenly, for no reason, great arrogance arises: arrogance is a form of pride – revering no one, slighting all, thinking no one equals him.

Thus pride arises – lofty self-pride, a very high kind of arrogance. Pride exceeding pride – extreme arrogance. Superiority pride – there is no higher form of pride than this – pride piled upon superiority pride, and inferiority pride: feeling everyone baser than himself and slighting them all. These are differing marks of pride, all arising at once.

In the mind even slighting the Tathagatas of the ten directions.

To what degree is he arrogant? Arrogant not only toward people but toward the Buddhas – slighting the Tathagatas, seeing them as not his equal. How grave when you utter such words.

How much more the lower ranks such as Hearers and Pratyekabuddhas: he slights these all the more, his attitude being: “You are nothing – mere Small-Vehicle Arhats – what is so good about you?”

He thought himself higher than the Buddhas – though unfortunately he never earned such a name.

Sutra text: Thử danh kiến thắng, vô huệ tự cứu. Ngộ tắc vô cữu, phi vi thánh chứng.

Translation: This is called holding a surpassing view, but lacking the wisdom to save oneself. Recognized, it is without fault – not sage realization.

Commentary: This is called holding a surpassing view – a state occurring incidentally within the feeling skandha – but lacking the wisdom to save oneself: such a person lacks the wisdom to rescue himself. Recognized, it is without fault: recognizing it as one's own delusion, demons get no chance to work – as people say: if you understand, you are not deluded; if you are deluded, you lack understanding. If you understand, it is like grasping the sword of wisdom severing all delusion.

That is not sage realization. This state is not sage realization – it is not that you have realized the sage fruition.

Sutra text: Nhược tác thánh giải, tắc hữu nhất phần, đại ngã mạn ma, nhập kì tâm phủ, bất lễ tháp miếu, tồi hủy kinh tượng. Vị đàn việt ngôn, thử thị toàn đồng, hoặc thị thổ mộc; kinh thị thụ diệp, hoặc thị chiên hoa; nhục thân chân thường, bất tự cung kính, khước sùng thổ mộc, thật vi điên đảo. Kì thâm tín giả, tòng kì hủy toái, mai khí địa trung. Nghi ngộ chúng sanh, nhập vô gián ngục. Thất ư chánh thọ, đương tòng luân trụy.

Translation: But if the cultivator claims sage realization, a kind of greatly arrogant demon enters the very heart: not bowing to stupas and temples, destroying sutras and images. Telling its donors that images are but bronze or clay and wood; sutras but tree leaves or silk; the flesh body truly constant, yet instead of revering itself, worshipping clay and wood – truly upside down.

Its deep believers follow its smashing, burying and abandoning them in the ground. For misleading beings with doubts and errors, they enter the uninterrupted hell. Losing right samadhi, they are sure to fall.

Commentary: But if the cultivator claims sage realization – thinking: “This is a good state” – then a greatly arrogant demon enters the very heart, possessing the body. Not bowing to stupas and temples: it does not bow to Buddhas or stupas, nor bow to Buddhas on entering temples. Destroying sutras and images: it burns sutras and smashes Buddha images – burning sutras and destroying images are karmic obstructions leading to the hells – yet it says: “these are all fakes.”

Telling its donors: it has close disciples and tells them so. Dan (Skt. dana) means giving; yue (越, Skt. pati) means crossing over. Hence in Buddhism those who make offerings to the Three Jewels are called dan-yue (donors). Demons also have their own donors and disciples. The demon tells these people:

These images are only gold, bronze, clay, wood… Sutras are only leaves, paper, silk.

Buddha images are made of gold, bronze, stuffed with clay, or carved of wood; sutras are written on leaves or on cloth and silk – what is worthy of worship in them? Why do you bow to such things? They are merely insentient objects.

This flesh body is truly real – this flesh body of mine is truly, eternally real – yet not revered: you do not revere this body of mine, but instead worship clay and wood.

What benefit is there in preferring to bow to wood and clay? What benefit in bowing to such idols? Better that you bow to me than to them.

Truly completely upside down: you bow to those idols, but they are only slabs of wood, insentient – how crazy to bow to them! Its deep believers in the demon – those deeply believing in the demon – follow its words, smashing Buddha images, burning sutras, burying them all in the ground. Through such conduct, for misleading beings with doubts and errors – making them disbelieve the Buddhadharma, doubtful and confused instead – sowing such doubts among beings, they are sure to fall into the uninterrupted hell. Losing right samadhi, they are sure to fall.

8 – BUOYANT EASE (THE DEMON OF EASE)

Sutra text: Hựu bỉ định trung, chư thiện nam tử, kiến sắc ấm tiêu, thọ ấm  minh bạch. Ư tinh minh trung, viên ngộ tinh lí, đắc đại tùy thuận. Kì tâm hốt sanh vô lượng khinh an. Dĩ ngôn thành thánh, đắc đại tự tại. Thử danh nhân huệ, hoạch chư khinh thanh. Ngộ tắc vô cữu, phi vi thánh chứng.

Translation: Further, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve and the feeling skandha clearly revealed – within the essential brightness, perfectly awakening to the subtle principle, gaining great compliance – the mind suddenly gives rise to boundless buoyant ease, claiming to have become a sage, gaining great self-mastery. This is called gaining lightness and clarity through wisdom. Recognized, it is without fault – not sage realization.

Commentary: Further, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve and the feeling skandha clearly revealed – within the essential brightness.

Awareness becomes bright and essential as never before. Perfectly awakening to the subtle, wondrous truth: the cultivator now gains penetrating understanding of the subtle, wondrous truths. Gaining great compliance: the mind suddenly attains boundless buoyant ease, claiming to have become a sage – a Buddha – gaining great self-mastery, attaining supreme bliss beyond all.

This is called: gaining lightness and clarity through wisdom – just opening a little wisdom, at once reaching a light, clear state, and that is all; surely nothing compared with the ultimate state.

Recognized, it is without fault – nothing is amiss. Not sage realization: you should not take this state for the sage fruition, for it is not.

Sutra text: Nhược tác thánh giải, tắc hữu nhất phần, hiếu thanh khinh ma, nhập kì tâm phủ. Tự vị mãn túc, cánh bất cầu tiến. Thửđẳng đa tác, Vô Văn  tỷ-khưu, nghi ngộ hậu sanh, đọa a-tì ngục. Thất ư chánh thọ, đương tòng luân trụy.

Translation: But if interpreted as sagehood, a kind of ease-loving demon enters the very heart, deeming itself complete, seeking no further advance. Such as these mostly act like the Unlearned Bhikshu, misleading later beings with doubts and errors, falling into the Avichi hell. Losing right samadhi, they are sure to fall.

Commentary: But if interpreted as sagehood – gaining this light, easy state and thinking oneself to have attained the sage fruition – then a kind of ease-loving demon enters the very heart: this kind of demon has also passed through the light, easy state and will possess such a person. Deeming itself complete – having accomplished everything – seeking no further advance: above, no Buddhahood to attain, for it is already a Buddha; nor need beings be saved, for the saving is already complete. It has attained Buddhahood as wished and saved beings in the sense it wished to save – hence seeking no advance at all.

Most such cultivators act like the Unlearned Bhikshu mentioned before: lacking wisdom, he mistook the Fourth Dhyana state for the fourth Arhat fruition.

Misleading later beings with doubts and errors: hence they do not recognize the true path nor understand the Buddhadharma – and for deluding and obstructing beings, they fall into the Avichi hell – in the future such people fall into the uninterrupted hell. Why? Losing right samadhi, they are sure to fall: once right samadhi is lost, the fall into the uninterrupted hell is certain.

9 – CLINGING TO EXTINCTION, DENYING CAUSE AND EFFECT

Sutra text: Hựu bỉ định trung, chư thiện nam tử, kiến sắc ấm tiêu, thọ ấm  minh bạch. Ư minh ngộ trung, đắc hư minh tánh. Kì trung hốt nhiên, quy hướng vĩnh diệt, bát vô cause and effect, nhất hướng nhập không. Không tâm hiện tiền, nãi chí tâm sanh trưởng đoạn diệt giải. Thử danh định tâm trầm một, thất ư chiếu ứng. Ngộ tắc vô cữu, phi vi thánh chứng.

Translation: Further, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve and the feeling skandha clearly revealed – within bright awakening, attaining an empty, bright nature – suddenly therein turning toward perpetual extinction, denying cause and effect, inclining wholly to emptiness. The empty mind manifesting, even giving rise to the understanding of eternal severance. This is called the settled mind sunk and lost, bereft of illumination. Recognized, it is without fault – not sage realization.

Commentary: Further, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve and the feeling skandha clearly revealed. Then within bright awakening – when one seems clear yet has not truly awakened – attaining an empty, bright nature: within that awakening attaining a kind of empty, bright light unable to ascertain reality. Suddenly therein turning toward perpetual extinction, denying cause and effect, taking everything as empty. Therein – within that empty brightness – a change suddenly occurs. What? The cultivator inclines toward extinction, denying cause and effect, taking all dharmas as empty.

It says: “When one dies, one is gone forever. So talk of cause and effect is mistaken: there is no cause and effect – at death nothing remains, so how could there be cause and effect? All dharmas are empty: creating offenses is empty, doing meritorious good is empty – all is empty.”

The empty mind manifesting, even growing the understanding of eternal severance.

The more it thinks, the more right it feels:

“Oh! Right – it is empty. Once you die, everything ends – all is empty!” Then it becomes convinced: everyone vanishes forever after death. The sutra text says: “Recognized, it is without fault – not the realization of sagehood.” A line quoted from a sutra whenever it is printed from the original – we should print this line appended.

This is called: “the settled mind scattered, bereft of illumination.”

The settled mind is now gone, hence thoughts clinging to emptiness arise, losing the ability to discern what is right. Recognized, it is without fault. That is not sage realization.

This is not the state of realizing the sage fruition.

Sutra text: Nhược tác thánh giải, tắc hữu không ma, nhập kì tâm phủ. Nãi báng trì giới, danh vi tiểu thừa, bồ-tát ngộ không, hữu hà trì phạm. Kì nhân thường ư, tín tâm đàn việt , ẩm tửu đạm nhục, quảng hành dâm uế. Nhân ma lực cố, nhiếp kì tiền nhân, bất sanh nghi báng. Quỷ tâm cửu nhập, hoặc thực thỉ niệu, dự tửu nhục đẳng, nhất chủng câu không. Phá Phật luật nghi, ngộ nhập nhân tội. Thất ư chánh thọ, đương tòng luân trụy.

Translation: But if interpreted as sagehood, a demon of emptiness enters the very heart. It then slanders precept-keeping, calling it the Small Vehicle, saying the Bodhisattva awakened to emptiness – what keeping or violating could there be? Such a person, at the homes of faithful donors, drinks wine, eats meat, and wantonly indulges in lust. Through demonic power it subdues those before it, who raise no doubt or slander. The ghost-mind long entered, it may eat excrement and urine, wine and meat together, taking all as equally empty – breaking the Buddha's moral code, misleading people into offenses. Losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

Commentary: But if interpreted as sagehood – taking this for sage-fruition realization – then a demon of emptiness enters the very heart: the demon enters possessing the cultivator's body. The demon then slanders precept-keepers, calling them “Small Vehicle.” The demon says:

“Do not keep precepts – that is the Small Vehicle Dharma. Great Vehicle Bodhisattvas should not be troubled by such restraints. You should not pay so much heed to those precepts.”

Or the demon says: “The great elephant does not walk the rabbit's path. The greatly awakened should not cling to trifles. Once you are greatly awakened, nothing concerns you anymore. All dharmas are empty. Did I not say this before? Wine and meat pass through the belly while the Buddha stays in the mind. All dharmas come from mind; mind is Buddha, Buddha is mind.”

Such is what the demon says. The demon further slanders precept-keepers:

“Only those clinging to the Small Vehicle keep precepts. Great Vehicle disciples do not bother with such matters.”

In fact, Buddhists cultivating the Great Vehicle keep the precepts most strictly – precept-violation is rare among them. The demon only deceives the ignorant – people who never study the Buddhadharma nor carefully investigate the principles the Buddha taught. That is why, whatever the demon says, they take as a command others must obey, forcing everyone to believe the demon's words true. Why do they believe the demon's words? Only because they have never heard the Buddhadharma taught – and even hearing, would they understand what the Buddhadharma is?

Saying: the Great Vehicle Bodhisattva awakened to the empty nature of dharmas – what keeping or violating could there be? Why keep holding the precepts or fear violating them? There are no such things. Such a person possessed by the demon, at the homes of faithful donors – Buddhist disciples who regularly support the Buddhadharma and trust it – drinks wine, eats meat, wantonly indulges in lust.

In the sutra text, wanton lustful indulgence is most significant: for Buddhism teaches people to have no lustful mind, yet its lustful mind grows. The demon even encourages lustful acts – and people still believe, for it has demonic power. Through demonic power it still subdues everyone, raising no doubt or slander – they believe it fanatically.

After the demon has entered the mind, it makes the person eat excrement, drink urine, eat meat and drink wine, taking all these as equally empty.

Since the cultivator is already demon-possessed, he does not know excrement unclean, and regularly drinks urine. It claims excrement and urine are “neither defiled nor pure,” borrowing phrases from the Prajna Sutra to argue falsely – misunderstanding the sutras' meaning. The demon behaves showing disregard for everything, clean or filthy alike – proclaiming eating meat and drinking wine empty, eating excrement and drinking urine empty: in short, taking all as empty.

It breaks the Buddha's moral code, misleading people into offenses. Then losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

10 – MAD GREEDY LOVE (THE DEMON OF GREEDY LOVE)

Sutra text: Hựu bỉ định trung, chư thiện nam tử, kiến sắc ấm tiêu, thọ ấm  minh bạch. Vị kì không minh, thâm nhập tâm cốt. Kì tâm hốt hữu vô hạn ái sanh. Ái cực phát cuồng, tiện vi tham dục. Thử danh định cảnh, an thuận nhập tâm, vô huệ tự trì, ngộ nhập chư dục. Ngộ tắc vô cữu, phi vi thánh chứng.

Translation: Further, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve and the feeling skandha clearly revealed – delighting in savoring that empty brightness, deeply entering to heart and bone – suddenly boundless love arises in the mind. Love carried to the extreme turns to madness, becoming greed and lust. This is called the samadhi-state settling smoothly into the mind, lacking the wisdom to restrain oneself, mistakenly entering the desires. Recognized, it is without fault – not sage realization.

Commentary: Further, when good men in this samadhi see the form skandha dissolve.

When the cultivator has attained samadhi within the scope of the feeling skandha – seeing the form skandha dissolve, the form skandha gone – the feeling skandha clearly revealed, clearly perceiving the feeling skandha. Delighting in savoring the empty brightness – the state the cultivator has realized – now deeply entering to heart and bone: a sudden psychological shift occurs. Suddenly boundless love arises in the mind – like someone saying: “I love everyone, and I love gossiping about such things.”

Love carried to the extreme turns to madness, becoming greed and lust. When love and craving rise to the extreme, the cultivator goes mad with lust. The cultivator cannot restrain his emotions; grown mad, the cultivator is like the woman Liu Jin-tong I spoke of before: on meeting men she embraced them, weeping and making seductive gestures – a textbook example of this kind of demon. How could an ordinary man keep his heart unmoved before such seduction? Having enchanted men, she would say: “Take this money and buy me that piece of jewelry.” He would answer “Yes, yes!” – then she told him to take money and buy her something else, and he obediently complied. Why? Simply because she satisfied the man's lust and he was deluded by demonic power. When love reaches the extreme, a man goes mad with greed and lust – lust arising from the greedy mind.

This is called the samadhi-state settling smoothly into the mind, lacking the wisdom to restrain oneself, hence deluded, indulging in the desires.

In samadhi there is a state of ease and contentment entering the mind, but lacking the wisdom to restrain one's emotions and cravings – ending in abandon to lustful desires.

Recognized, it is without fault.

This is only a temporary, incidental state. The cultivator should recognize this state as a demonic state, and not sage realization. If you understand, very good – what is fearful is when you do not recognize the demonic state you are sunk in. You will fall into an enchanting maze with no way out.

Sutra text: Nhược tác thánh giải, tắc hữu dục ma nhập kì tâm phủ. Nhất hướng thuyết dục, vi bồ-đề đạo. Hóa chư bạch y, bình đẳng hành dục, kì hành dâm giả, danh trì pháp tử. Thần quỷ lực cố, ư mạt thế trung, nhiếp kì phàm ngu, kì số chí bách, như thị nãi chí, nhất bách nhị bách, hoặc ngũ lục bách, đa mãn thiên vạn. Ma tâm sanh yểm, li kì thân thể. Oai đức kí vô, hãm ư vương nạn. Nghi ngộ chúng sanh, nhập vô gián ngục. Thất ư chánh thọ, đương tòng luân trụy.

Translation: But if interpreted as sagehood, a demon of lust enters the very heart: ever proclaiming lust the Bodhi Way, teaching lay followers to practice lust equally, calling its lust-practitioners Dharma-heirs. Through ghosts' and spirits' power, in the Dharma-ending age it gathers ordinary fools – a hundred, even one or two hundred, or five or six hundred, many up to thousands upon myriads. When the demon mind grows weary, it leaves the body; prestige and virtue gone, one falls into legal peril. Misleading beings with doubts and errors, one enters the uninterrupted hell. Losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

Commentary: But if you claim to be a sage – then a demon of lust enters the heart. If the cultivator takes this for sage-fruition realization, through mistaken views a demon of lust and craving enters the mind, possessing the body. Ever proclaiming lust the Bodhi Way – it becomes an all-out advocate of lust, calling it the Bodhi Way.

It will say: “Apart from lust there is nothing.”

Just as in America there is a sect advocating polygamy, holding “the more wives the better.” This sect is exactly like that kind of demon – encouraging and enticing lustful craving by saying: “Very good to have many wives – nothing grave in it. That is the Bodhi Way – the more wives the better.”

It teaches lay followers to practice lust equally, calling its lust-practitioners Dharma-heirs. It teaches disciples to practice lust equally, saying: “Make no distinctions between this person and that – enjoy pleasure together.” Regardless of one's own wife or another's, they simply act on fancy. In America there is a bizarre wife-swapping fad: a place where people go to exchange wives with one another – just like the deeds of the demon discussed in the sutra.

Calling its lust-practitioners Dharma-heirs: those joining in lust with it are called keepers of the Dharma-seed, continuers of the Dharma transmitted by the demon.

Through demonic power, in the Dharma-ending age, it draws and deludes disciples from among ordinary fools – a hundred, even five or six hundred, up to thousands upon myriads. At last when the demon king grows weary – what do you think happens? It abandons the person. What happens when the demon leaves? The person no longer has spiritual powers.

When the demon's alluring power is gone, one falls into legal peril.

Its alluring power came from spiritual powers – the demon king had spiritual powers. But now the demon king has left, so the person has no more spiritual powers. Do you know what happens? He violates the nation's laws: before, while he still had spiritual powers, the demon king could help him evade national law and keep the authorities from learning of the matter. But with the demon king gone, this ordinary fellow is back to normal – a lawbreaker. People recognize him as a master of heterodox side-doors, habitually cheating and deceiving students with bizarre mantras and spells. Violating the law, he is arrested and jailed.

For misleading beings with doubts and errors, never meeting the true Way, one falls into the uninterrupted hell – surely falling into the Avichi hell. Why? For losing right samadhi, one is sure to fall.

THE WORLD-HONORED ONE'S CONCLUDING EXHORTATION ON THE FEELING SKANDHA

Sutra text: A-nan, như thị thập chủng thiền-na hiện cảnh, giai thị thọ ấm , dụng tâm giao hỗ, cố hiện tư sự. Chúng sanh ngoan mê, bất tự thốn lượng, phùng thử nhân duyên, mê bất tự thức, vị ngôn đăng thánh, đại vọng ngữ thành đọa vô gián ngục.

Translation: Ananda, these ten states appearing in dhyana all come from the feeling skandha and the mind's applied effort interweaving, hence these occurrences. Obstinate and deluded beings, not assessing themselves, encountering such conditions, deluded and unaware, claim to have ascended to sagehood – committing the great falsehood, they fall into the uninterrupted hell.

Commentary: Ananda, these ten states appearing in dhyana all come from the feeling skandha and the mind's applied effort interweaving, hence these occurrences.

Ananda! Such states manifesting while cultivating dhyana all lie within the scope of the feeling skandha interweaving with vigorous effort in practice. These events result from various transformations occurring while the cultivator applies vigorous effort.

Obstinate beings, deluded and confused, do not assess themselves.

Beings, deluded, do not turn back to contemplate within themselves.

Encountering such conditions, deluded and unaware.

Beings do not recognize who they are.

Claiming to have realized the sage rank.

Then they claim to have attained what they never attained and realized what they never realized – proclaiming to have attained the Way and realized the sage rank, when they never attained such things at all.

Thus incurring the offense of the great falsehood. Surely falling into the uninterrupted hell.

Sutra text: Nhữ đẳng diệc đương, tương Như Lai ngữ, ư ngã diệt hậu, truyền thị mạt pháp, biến linh chúng sanh khai ngộ tư nghĩa. Vô linh thiên ma đắc kì phương tiện. Bảo trì phúc hộ, thành vô thượng đạo.

Translation: After my extinction, you should transmit the Tathagata's words, proclaiming them in the Dharma-ending age, so that all beings awaken to these meanings. Do not let the heavenly demons gain their advantage. Protect and shelter beings, accomplishing the unsurpassed Way.

Commentary: After the Tathagata's extinction into nirvana, you should transmit the Tathagata's words, so that beings of the Dharma-ending age all awaken to these meanings.

Ananda, after the Tathagata enters nirvana, you should transmit the Tathagata's words – proclaim the words the Tathagata taught.

So that beings of the Dharma-ending age all awaken to these meanings – enabling beings to hear the principles, understand, and awaken.

Do not let the heavenly demons gain their advantage. Do not let demons get a convenient chance to disturb cultivators.

Protect and shelter beings in cultivation until the unsurpassed Way is accomplished.

VOLUME 9 (PART 5): THE TEN DEMONIC STATES OF THE THINKING SKANDHA

Brief Commentary on the Shurangama Sutra — Venerable Master Hsuan Hua

THE SHURANGAMA SUTRA

THE FIFTY SKANDHA-DEMONS

Lectured by Venerable Master Hsuan Hua at

The Buddhist Lecture Hall, San Francisco

THE THINKING SKANDHA

THE MENTAL STATE BEFORE ENTERING THE THINKING SKANDHA

Sutra text: A-nan, bỉ thiện nam tử, tu tam-ma-đề, thọ ấm tận giả, tuy vị lậu tận, tâm li kì hình, như điểu xuất lung. Dĩ năng thành tựu, tùng thị phàm thân, thượng lịch bồ-tát lục thập thánh vị, đắc ý sanh thân, tùy vãng vô ngại.

Translation: Ananda, that good man cultivating samadhi, with the feeling skandha exhausted, though not yet beyond outflow, his mind can leave the body as a bird escapes its cage. Having accomplished this, from this ordinary body he can pass through the Bodhisattvas' sixty holy stages, attaining the mind-made body, going and coming without obstruction.

Commentary: Ananda, that good man cultivating samadhi, with the feeling skandha exhausted – when the feeling skandha is purified. Though not yet beyond outflow, his mind can leave the body as a bird escapes its cage. Though delusion is not yet exhausted, he already has a little spiritual power: the mind can leave the body as a bird escapes its cage.

Before, the cultivator attaining only to the exhaustion of the feeling skandha was like one locked tight within his bodily shell – exactly like a bird locked in a cage. Now the bird can escape the cage.

Having accomplished this, from this ordinary body he can pass through the Bodhisattvas' sixty holy stages.

From the ordinary body having accomplished this – that is, having a little spiritual power – he can pass through the sixty holy stages of the Bodhisattvas: right in the ordinary body, the cultivator can become a Bodhisattva, realizing the sixty holy stages of the Bodhisattvas.

Attaining the mind-made body, going and coming without obstruction.

The cultivator must clearly establish earnest, diligent effort in practice before gaining the spiritual power of the mind-made body. Attaining this body, the cultivator can go wherever he wishes.

What are the Bodhisattvas' sixty holy stages? They are the fifty-five stages taught in the earlier section, plus the three gradual steps, plus the Dry Wisdom Ground and Wondrous Awakening – sixty holy stages in all.

THE SCOPE OF THE THINKING SKANDHA

Sutra text: Thí như hữu nhân, thục mị nghệ ngôn. Thị nhân tuy tắc, vô biệt sở tri, kì ngôn dĩ thành, âm vận luân thứ, linh bất mị giả, hàm ngộ kì ngữ. Thử tắc danh vi, tưởng âm khu vũ.

Translation: It is like a person talking in his sleep in deep slumber: though the person knows nothing else, his words are already formed – cadenced, ordered in sequence – so that those not asleep all understand his speech. This is called the region of the thinking skandha.

Commentary: Like a person talking in his sleep in deep slumber: this is a comparison – the scope of the thinking skandha is like one talking deliriously in deep sleep: asleep, he begins saying whatever he wants to say. Though the person knows nothing of what he says, his words are already formed – cadenced and coherent: though the cultivator knows nothing of what he says in deep sleep, what he says is coherent, flowing in a logical sequence, clearly meaningful – yet he knows nothing of what he has said. But those not asleep all understand.

For example, the person says: “Today I want to eat bean curd, so I went to the shop and bought ten slabs. Returning home, I steamed the cakes and ate them.”

He knows nothing of what he has said – but the others awake know very well: “Oh, today he ate bean curd.”

Why does he say such things? Because he has not forgotten what he ate – he still remembers the eating, so he mentions it even in dreams.

This is the region of the thinking skandha.

It is analogous to the territory of the thinking skandha. But do not take this so simply as to say: “The thinking skandha is just talking deliriously in sleep” – quite mistaken to infer so. This is only an analogy.

THE ROOT OF THE THINKING SKANDHA

Sutra text: Nhược động niệm tận, phù tưởng tiêu trừ. Ư giác minh tâm, như khử trần cấu. Nhất luân  sanh tử, thủ vĩ viên chiếu, danh tưởng ấm tận. Thị nhân tắc năng, siêu phiền não trược. Quán kì sở do, dung thông vọng tưởng, dĩ vi kì bản.

Translation: When stirring thoughts are exhausted and floating thoughts removed, within the awakened bright mind, as if dust and defilement cleansed away – one stream of birth and death, head and tail roundly illumined – this is called the exhaustion of the thinking skandha. Such a person can then transcend the defilement of afflictions. Contemplate its cause: interfused false thought is its root.

Commentary: When stirring thoughts are exhausted, floating, coarse thoughts removed. The extremely subtle false thoughts are in the sixth consciousness; eliminating the floating, coarse false thoughts – since these subtle thoughts in the sixth consciousness have been removed, the coarse, false, floating thoughts are removed along with them.

Within the awakened bright mind, as if dust and defilement cleansed away. This awakened bright mind is the eighth consciousness – now clearly the eighth consciousness has purified all defilement of false dust.

One stream of birth and death, head and tail roundly illumined: there are twelve kinds of beings – from the womb-born and egg-born to the neither-thinking-nor-not-thinking – and the cultivator clearly knows the causes planted before and the results to be undergone after, of every kind of being.

That is called the exhaustion of the thinking skandha. When the cultivator attains the power of knowing past lives, such a person can transcend the defilement of afflictions.

Contemplate the cause of the thinking skandha – contemplating the deep cause of all the cultivator's creations. Its root is interfused false thought.

By this point, false thoughts have become interfused with one another, each false thought becoming the source of itself.

THE STATES OF THE THINKING SKANDHA

* * *

1 – GREED FOR SKILLFUL MEANS

Sutra text: A-nan, bỉ thiện nam tử, thọ ấm hư diệu, bất tao tà lự, viên định phát minh, tam ma địa trung, tâm ái viên minh, nhuệ kì tinh tư, tham cầu thiện xảo.

Translation: Ananda, when the feeling skandha has become empty and wondrous, no longer subject to deviant concerns – the perfect samadhi disclosed – within samadhi the mind longs for perfect brightness, urging thought onward, greedily seeking skillful means.

Commentary: Ananda, when the feeling skandha has become empty and wondrous, no longer entangled in deviant concerns – not a single evil thought can stir the cultivator anymore.

The perfect samadhi disclosed, within samadhi – the mind longs for perfect brightness, urging thought onward, greedily seeking skillful means.

Urging means excessively refining the inward contemplation of the mind – also the state of perfect brightness. The cultivator longs for skillful means to teach beings, and the greedy mind thus arises.

Sutra text: Nhĩ thời thiên ma, hậu đắc kì tiện, phi tinh phụ nhân, khẩu thuyết kinh pháp.

Translation: Then the heavenly demon, waiting for its convenient chance, sends its essence to possess another person, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

Commentary: Then the heavenly demon (of the Six Desire heavens) waits for its convenient chance: knowing the cultivator's samadhi power is nearly complete, it waits for a convenient opening to possess. It watches for some trait in the cultivator to open the way in: when the cultivator's samadhi power lacks firmness, the entrance appears. Once the cultivator gives rise to a false thought, samadhi power is no longer firm and the heavenly demon at once gets its chance to possess – hence “the demon gets a convenient chance.”

Sending its essence to possess another person, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

The heavenly demon orders its followers: “Go there and destroy that cultivator's samadhi power.” Before the form and feeling skandhas are exhausted, the heavenly demon possesses and harasses the cultivator himself. But after the form and feeling skandhas dissolve and the cultivator reaches the scope of the thinking skandha, the heavenly demon can no longer possess the cultivator; it must possess someone else's body, then preach the Dharma to that cultivator through the mouth of the one whose body the demon has seized. That person lectures Sutras, but the Dharma he lectures is deviant Dharma – so you must recognize that error.

Sutra text: Kì nhân bất giác, thị  kỳ ma trước, tự ngôn vị đắc vô thượng niết-bàn. Lai bỉ cầu xảo, thiện nam tử xứ, phu tòa thuyết pháp. Kỳ hình tư tu, hoặc tác tỷ-khưu, linh bỉ nhân kiến, hoặc vi Đế thích , hoặc vi phụ nữ, hoặc tỷ-khưu ni, hoặc tẩm ám thất, thân hữu quang minh.

Translation: That person, unaware he is possessed by a demon, claims to have attained unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the good man seeking skillful means, it spreads its seat and preaches the Dharma. In a moment its form transforms – appearing as a bhikshu, letting that person see; or as Shakra, or as a woman, or as a bhikshuni; or lying in a dark room, its body emitting light.

Commentary: You can see how harmful it is to meet this demonic state.

That person truly does not know he is demon-possessed – how absurd that a demon should come “help” him. Claiming to have attained unsurpassed nirvana: he proclaims he has gained the wondrous fruition of nirvana.

When the demon comes to the place of the good man seeking skillful means, spreading its seat, preaching the Dharma for the good man longing for skillful means to hear.

In a moment – very quickly – it can transform, appearing as a bhikshu, letting the good man see – appearing as Shakra (King of Gods), a woman, or a bhikshuni. When the good man seeking skillful means sees such transformations, he thinks: “He must be Guanyin Bodhisattva” – never knowing it is a heavenly demon. That is why you should cling to no state you realize, whatever state it may be.

Or lying in a dark room, its body emitting light: when one ignorant of the Buddhadharma sees this, he marvels: “Oh, his body emits light – if he is not a Buddha, he must at least be a Bodhisattva or an Arhat.” They do not recognize the person as demon-possessed, the demon king displaying spiritual powers to delude the cultivator.

Therefore, until the cultivator clearly and thoroughly understands the Buddhadharma truly, he should not let himself be turned by whatever state he sees. Do not be swayed by those states. How should you deal with such a state? Regard it as if nothing existed – as if never seen. If you grow excited on seeing demons, you will be turned by demonic states. How then should you act? Simply maintain the spirit of the Middle Way – neither liking nor disliking, seeing as if never seen, hearing as if never heard. You should not think: “How marvelous – I wish to meet it again.” With such a thought, you at once fall into error.

Sutra text: Thị nhân ngu mê, hoặc vi bồ-tát. Tín kì giáo hóa, diêu đãng kì tâm, phá Phật luật nghi, tiềm hành tham dục.

Translation: That person, deluded, mistakes it for a Bodhisattva. Believing its teaching, his mind is swayed; breaking the Buddha's moral code, he secretly practices greed and lust.

Commentary: That person cultivating right samadhi, deluded at this point, mistakes it for a Bodhisattva: seeing one who can appear as a bhikshu, Shakra, a laywoman, or a bhikshuni, or suddenly change from one person to another, the cultivator deems this person surely a Bodhisattva. Then believing the demon's teaching, his mind is swayed, breaking the Buddha's moral code.

What should we observe in a cultivator? See whether he keeps the Buddha's precepts: if he does not uphold them, he is surely a demon; if he strictly keeps the precepts, he is truly a Bodhisattva. Yet some call themselves Buddhists, style themselves Elder Sangha Masters, piling on still more titles.

And secretly practicing greed and lust: secretly committing lustful acts, striving to hide them from people.

Sutra text: Khẩu trung hảo ngôn tai tường biến dị, hoặc ngôn Như Lai, mỗ xứ xuất thế, hoặc ngôn kiếp hỏa, hoặc thuyết đao binh. Khủng bố ư nhân, linh kì gia tư, vô cố hao tán.

Translation: Its mouth delights in speaking of calamities and anomalies – saying a Tathagata has appeared in some place, or speaking of eon-fires, or of wars and weapons – terrifying people, causing them to pointlessly squander their family wealth.

Commentary: That person possessed by the demon delights in speaking of calamitous anomalies, strange upheavals.

What does the possessed person love to speak of? They love speaking of disasters and tragic upheavals – telling of every calamity sure to occur exactly somewhere, or an auspicious omen occurring somewhere, or an unusual upheaval about to befall.

Or saying a Tathagata has appeared in some place.

He says: “Do you know – that Buddha, of such a name, has already appeared in the world over there!”

Or speaking of the tragedy of eon-fires, or speaking of wars and weapons: he says: “The three calamities – water, fire, wind – and the eight difficulties have come upon us!”

Or saying: “This eon is about to perish.” Or threatening that war is about to break out here, or that Russia is about to go to war with this or that country.

Terrifying people, causing them to pointlessly squander their family wealth.

He constantly says things to draw people's attention, then unsettles them: once people hear such news, they panic: “Oh! No! War is coming – my life is in danger!”

Or the demon says: “War is coming. If you hand money to me at once, I shall guarantee your life safe; if you do not give me money, you will lose your life.” It always speaks so to cheat people.

If you wish to tell who is genuine and who is false – whether someone is a Bodhisattva or a heavenly demon – you need only look at these points: first, see whether the person has a mind of lust; second, see whether the person craves money. If the person cheats people to satisfy greed for wealth and fondness for beauty, that person is not genuine. What is greed for wealth? For example, the person may say: “A great disaster is about to befall us – the world is coming to its end. An atom bomb is about to explode over there; an H-bomb is about to drop on that place.”

Speaking so, making people panic, then bringing money to offer it. If you stay alert to its tricks – even if it emits light, shakes the earth, or does other extraordinary things – you should not believe it, for it has a greedy mind. One without a greedy mind is genuine; one greedy is false. The method I now teach is practical and tested.

Sutra text: Thử danh quái quỷ, niên lão thành ma, não loạn thị nhân. Yểm túc tâm sanh, khứ bỉ nhân thể. Đệ tử dữ sư, câu hãm vương nạn.

Translation: This is called a strange ghost, aged into a demon, harassing this person. Sated after its disturbance, it arises and leaves that person's body. Both disciple and teacher fall into legal peril.

Commentary: This is called a strange ghost, living a long time, aged into a demon – specializing in harassing cultivators. Sated after its disturbance, it arises and leaves the possessed person's body: at last it tires of this game – having seen enough, it stops possessing others. When this happens, both disciple and teacher fall into legal peril – wanted by the authorities, accused of inciting the masses, liable to execution or equivalent prison terms.

Sutra text: Nhữ đương tiên giác, bất nhập luân hồi. Mê hoặc bất tri, đọa vô gián ngục.

Translation: You should be awakened beforehand, and not enter the turning wheel. Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

Commentary: You should be awakened beforehand, and not enter the demon king's turning wheel of birth and death – you must awaken to this early, and not fall into the demon king's wheel of birth and death.

Deluded and unknowing, in the future one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

2 – FOND OF TRAVELING

Sutra text: A-nan, hựu thiện nam tử, thọ ấm  hư diệu, bất tao tà lự. Viên định phát minh, tam-ma-địa trung, tâm ái du đãng, phi kì tinh tư, tham cầu kinh lịch.

Translation: Ananda, again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed – within samadhi the mind fond of roaming, letting thought fly out, greedily seeking to travel about.

Commentary: Ananda, again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns. In the empty, penetrating, wondrous state gained after the feeling skandha has dissolved – the cultivator cultivating samadhi no longer has deviant concerns – disclosed, dwelling in the bright, perfect samadhi. Within samadhi the mind has false thoughts fond of roaming.

That is “exiting through the crown of the head and wandering with the soul” – the soul roaming everywhere: hence thought flies out, greedily seeking to roam. Letting the spirit fly out, wishing to go everywhere sightseeing at ease.

Sutra text: Nhĩ thời thiên ma, hầu đắc kì tiện, phi tinh phụ nhân, khẩu thuyết kinh pháp.

Translation: Then the heavenly demon, waiting for its convenient chance, sends its essence to possess another person, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

Commentary: Then the heavenly demon waits for its convenient chance: the demon king in the heavens again grows jealous, waiting for a lapse to possess.

Sending its essence to possess another person – again sending a trusted follower to possess that person. Using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma: it comes to harass the cultivator. Why is the cultivator possessed by demons? Simply because he greedily seeks roaming, wishing to travel and wander about: the moment he gives rise to the thought longing to roam, he at once gives the heavenly demon a convenient chance to torment him. Demons can possess nowhere unless the cultivator gives rise to such greedy false thoughts.

Sutra text: Kì nhân diệc bất giác tri ma trước, diệc ngôn tự đắc, vô thượng niết-bàn. Lai bỉ cầu du, thiện nam tử xứ, phu tòa thuyết pháp, tự hình vô biến. Kì thính pháp giả, hốt tự kiến thân, tọa bảo liên hoa, toàn thể hóa thành, tử kim quang tụ. Nhất chúng thính nhân, các các như thị, đắc vị tằng hữu.

Translation: That person, likewise unaware of demonic possession, likewise claims to have attained unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the good man seeking to roam, it spreads its seat and preaches the Dharma, its own form unchanged. But its listeners suddenly see themselves seated on jeweled lotuses, their whole bodies transformed into masses of purple-golden light. Each listener alike, gaining what never was.

Commentary: That person, likewise unaware of demonic possession, likewise claiming to have attained unsurpassed Bodhi – proclaiming to have reached the wondrous fruition of unsurpassed nirvana. When the demon comes to the place of the one seeking to roam – the good man who has given rise to the false thought wishing his spirit to exit through the crown of his head and go wandering –
