The demon spreads its seat, preaching the Dharma, its own preaching form unchanged.

In the sutra passage lectured before, the possessed person's body transformed into a bhikshu, bhikshuni, Shakra, laywoman, or countless other shapes. But in this case the demon-possessed person's body does not change. There are many kinds of demons, and you should not mistake ordinary matters for wholesome Dharma: if that happens and you do not recognize it correctly, demons will possess you at once.

But its listeners suddenly see themselves seated on jeweled lotus thrones, their whole bodies transformed into masses of purple-golden light.

Suddenly everyone feels as if seated on a jeweled lotus throne, the whole body transformed into a mass of blazing purple-golden color.

Every listener feels so, deeming themselves to have gained what never was.

Sutra text: Thị nhân ngu mê, hoặc vi bồ-tát, dâm dật kì tâm, phá Phật luật nghi, tiềm hành tham dục.

Translation: That person, deluded, mistakes it for a Bodhisattva; the mind turned lustful, breaking the Buddha's moral code, secretly practicing greed and lust.

Commentary: That person, deluded, mistakes it for a Bodhisattva.

Not only this person – all the listeners are very deluded, their minds grown doubtful, thinking: “He must be a Bodhisattva – he can make me sit on a seven-jeweled lotus throne and turn my body into a mass of blazing purple-golden color.”

You should ask yourselves: “Am I truly seated on a lotus throne blazing purple-golden?” How could you, in an ordinary body, have such a state? Is this not a heavenly demon come to delude? Why would a Bodhisattva display such a state? What is that Bodhisattva possessing you for?

The mind turned lustful.

The minds of those hearing its sutra-lectures grow unsettled, beginning to give rise to lustful thoughts.

Breaking the Buddha's moral code.

They no longer keep the Buddha's precepts. You must all remember: after receiving the precepts, do not be deceived by such deluding states. Even if a Dharma master displays great spiritual powers, you must observe him carefully to see whether he has a greedy mind: if he craves money or harbors lust, he is not one with a true mind – he is a fraud. But if the person no longer has lust or greed, hiding no inner designs, he is genuine. If he destroys the Buddha's precepts, he is a cheat.

Secretly practicing lustful acts.

Indulging wantonly, dissolutely, in secret.

Sutra text: Khẩu trung hảo ngôn, chư Phật ứng thế. Mỗ xứ mỗ nhân, đương thị mỗ Phật, hóa thân lai thử. Mỗ nhân tức thị, mỗ bồ-tát đẳng lai hóa nhân gian. Kì nhân kiến cố, tâm sanh khát ngưỡng, tà kiến mật hưng, chủng trí tiêu diệt.

Translation: Its mouth delights in saying Buddhas are appearing in the world: that person, that place, is precisely such a Buddha, manifesting its transformation-body here; that person is precisely such a Bodhisattva come to teach the human realm. On seeing this, that person gives rise to thirsting admiration; wrong views secretly flourish, and the seed-wisdom is destroyed.

Commentary: Its mouth delights in saying Buddhas are appearing in the world. The demon's mouth loves saying Buddhas are manifesting here and there.

The possessed person loves wandering about, then exploits that roaming to speak of mysterious, uncanny things – things he says so fantastically people hardly believe. He says: “Now Buddhas are manifesting in the world to save beings.”

He says that person, that place, is precisely such a Buddha, manifesting its transformation-body – that Buddha has manifested in the world in that person, at that place.

It says he is precisely such-and-such a Buddha… manifesting at that place to save all beings. Or saying that person is precisely a Bodhisattva manifesting here to teach the human realm.

For example, a disciple of mine named Gary (Cát-lợi) reported: Samalosa (?) said his teacher (Samalosa) is a Bodhisattva. How absurd! What kind of Bodhisattva? A demon-Bodhisattva? They only deceive people. I shall tell you plainly: a Buddha or a Bodhisattva never claims to be a Buddha or Bodhisattva – still less lets his disciples go advertising him.

“My teacher is a Bodhisattva” – never speak of your teacher so. Why would you say your teacher is a Buddha? Never speak of me so. Have I not told you I am a demon? Speak of your teacher only as a demon. I do not wish to be called a Buddha or Bodhisattva. How pitiable these people are! Here they say: “This is a Bodhisattva manifesting to teach beings in the Dharma-ending age.”

On seeing this, the cultivator gives rise to thirsting admiration.

Because such people have immature understanding, not truly understanding the Buddhadharma. They think:

“Oh! He is a Bodhisattva – wonderful! Quickly go hear him lecture and ask to become his disciple.”

As yesterday, when some people came to steal the Dharma by listening: I asked who their teacher was, and they answered so-and-so… That is a case in point. Their minds brim with thirsting admiration.

“I should ask that Bodhisattva to be my teacher, and draw near to learn the Bodhisattva Dharma from him.”

Since he is a Bodhisattva, of course disciples learning from him will also become Bodhisattvas – as a necessary result.

Wrong views secretly flourish: gradually wrong views grow thicker, and the seed-wisdom is destroyed.

Seed-wisdom – the Buddha's and all kinds of wisdom – is destroyed; the seeds of wisdom destroyed – truly perilous.

Sutra text: Thử danh bạt quỷ, niên lão thành ma, não loạn thị nhân, yểm túc tâm sanh, khứ bỉ nhân thể. Đệ tử dữ sư, câu hãm vương nạn.

Translation: This is called a drought-ghost, aged into a demon, harassing this person; sated, it arises and leaves that person's body. Both disciple and teacher fall into legal peril.

Commentary: This is called a drought-ghost, aged into a demon.

Wherever this kind of drought-ghost goes, there is no rain – drought lasting at least six months, sometimes one, two, or five years. Wherever this demon goes, there is no rain. When young, it is called a demon; grown old, it grows more vicious and treacherous, turning into a ghost. There is an ancient saying:

“Growing old without dying makes one a villain” – old yet undying is cunning. All the more cunning for a ghost: a demon old yet undying turns into a ghost.

It harasses the cultivator. Sated after a time.

After playing its cheating game a long time, the demon tires of it – nothing amusing anymore. It arises and leaves the possessed person's body. Then both teacher and disciple fall into legal peril – both arrested and jailed, liable to execution or life imprisonment – life as if in hell.

Sutra text: Nhữ đương tiên giác, bất nhập luân hồi. Mê hoặc bất tri, đọa vô gián ngục.

Translation: You should be awakened beforehand, and not enter the turning wheel. Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

Commentary: You should be awakened beforehand, and not enter the turning wheel – within the demon king's wheel, not becoming the demon king's retinue. Deluded and unknowing: failing to recognize the demon king's deeds, one follows the demon king, falling into the uninterrupted hell.

3 – GREED FOR UNION

Sutra text: Hựu thiện nam tử, thọ ấm  hư diệu, bất tao tà lự. Viên định phát minh, tam-ma-địa trung, tâm ái miên vẫn, trừng kì tinh tư,  tham cầu  khế hợp.

Translation: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed – within samadhi the mind fond of hidden accord, settling thought, greedily seeking union.

Commentary: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed.

Again, in the empty, penetrating, wondrous state gained after the feeling skandha has dissolved, the cultivator no longer has deviant concerns, dwelling in the bright, perfect samadhi. Within samadhi, the mind fond of hidden accord – the mind fond of spiritual union.

The mind wishes to draw near the holy sages. Settling thought, greedily seeking union: the cultivator strives to settle the mind, reaching purity. Because of a hidden thought greedily seeking union, the cultivator has given the demon king a fine chance to destroy him.

Sutra text: Nhĩ thời thiên ma, hậu đắc kì tiện, phi tinh phụ nhân, khẩu thuyết kinh pháp.

Translation: Then the heavenly demon gets its convenient chance, sending its essence to possess another person, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

Commentary: Then the heavenly demon gets its convenient chance. Sending its essence to possess another person, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

The heavenly demon sees its convenient chance, and so swiftly sends its essence to possess that person, using his mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

Sutra text: Kì nhân diệc bất giác tri ma trước, diệc ngôn tự đắc, vô thượng niết-bàn. Lai bỉ cầu hợp thiện nam tử xứ, phu tòa thuyết pháp. Kì hình cập bỉ, thính pháp chi nhân, ngoại vô thiên biến, linh kì thính giả, vị văn pháp tiền, tâm tự khai ngộ. Niệm niệm  di dịch, hoặc đắc túc mệnh, hoặc hữu tha tâm, hoặc kiến the hell realms, hoặc tri nhân gian, hảo ác chư sự, hoặc khẩu thuyết kệ, hoặc tự tụng kinh. Các các hoan ngu, đắc vị tằng hữu.

Translation: That person, likewise unaware of demonic possession, likewise claims to have attained unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the good man seeking union, it spreads its seat and preaches the Dharma. Its form and those listening to the Dharma show no outward change – yet it makes its listeners, before hearing the Dharma, feel their minds self-awakened – thought after thought shifting – some gaining knowledge of past lives, some possessing knowledge of others' minds, some seeing the hells, some knowing good and evil matters in the human realm, some speaking verses from the mouth, some reciting sutras of themselves. Each rejoicing, gaining what never was.

Commentary: That possessed person, likewise unaware of demonic possession, likewise claiming to have attained the wondrous fruition of unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the good man seeking spiritual union, at once spreading the Dharma seat, mounting it, preaching the Dharma. The form of that person and of the Dharma-listeners outwardly shows no change.

Its bodily form and the Dharma-listeners' show no change – nothing happening to the outside of their bodies. This passage differs from the earlier sutra passage, where listeners suddenly saw themselves seated on jeweled lotus thrones or saw their bodies emitting blazing purple-golden light; nor like seeing the preacher transform into Shakra, bhikshus, bhikshunis, women. In this case there is no such transformation.

But instead, it makes its listeners, before hearing the Dharma, feel “awakened.” After that awakened feeling, they feel as if just sobered from drink or just awakened from a dream in which they grew rich. This awakened feeling is not true awakening – only a kind of illusion, like watching a movie or taking a hallucinogenic pill. They see everything in phantasmal transformation, so their thought after thought shifts.

Some gain knowledge of past lives – though that knowledge of past lives is also unreal; all they see is illusion. Some possess knowledge of others' minds, or see all the states of the hells, or know good and evil matters in the human realm, or can speak verses in their own style at will, or recite sutras on impulse. Everyone rejoices, feeling as gaining what never was.

They all say: “He is truly a Bodhisattva – he is a Buddha – he awakened me, he gave me knowledge of past lives.” Yet that feeling lasts only while they listen to the demon lecture the Dharma – that is the key telling you the Dharma is not true.

Sutra text: Thị nhân ngu mê, hoặc vi bồ-tát, miên ái kì tâm, phá Phật luật nghi, tiềm hành tham dục.

Translation: That person, deluded, mistakes it for a Bodhisattva; the mind entangled in fond love, breaking the Buddha's moral code, secretly practicing greed and lust.

Commentary: That person, deluded, mistakes it for a Bodhisattva: that person is extremely deluded, imagining the possessed one a Bodhisattva. The mind entangled in fond love: he befriends the demon, breaking the Buddha's moral code, no longer observing the precepts. Secretly practicing greed and lust: quietly committing lustful acts.

Sutra text: Khẩu trung hiếu ngôn, Phật hữu đại tiểu;mỗ Phật tiên Phật, mỗ Phật hậu Phật. Kì trung diệc hữu chân Phật giả Phật, nam Phật nữ Phật; bồ-tát diệc nhiên. Kì nhân kiến cố, tẩy địch bản tâm, dị nhập tà ngộ.

Translation: Its mouth delights in saying: Buddhas great and small; this Buddha first, that Buddha after; among them true Buddhas and false Buddhas, male Buddhas and female Buddhas; Bodhisattvas likewise. On seeing this, that person washes away his inherent mind, easily entering deviant awakening.

Commentary: It delights in saying: Buddhas great and small.

What does the demon love to say? It says: “You have studied the Buddhadharma – but do you know what Buddhas are? There are great Buddhas and small Buddhas, old Buddhas, young Buddhas,” explaining in further detail.

This Buddha is first, that Buddha after; this Buddha true, that Buddha false: the demon proclaims itself the true Buddha while the others are false Buddhas. It further speaks of male Buddhas, female Buddhas, insisting “the union of male and female produces Buddhas – that is the Buddhas' origin, that is the Bodhi mind.”

Of course this deludes people: they think “Oh, that is how one becomes a Buddha,” then abandon themselves to dissolute, depraved living – preferring death to a life without wanton lust.

It distinguishes Bodhisattvas likewise.

The demon keeps saying: “There are great Bodhisattvas, small Bodhisattvas, male Bodhisattvas, female Bodhisattvas.” In fact – unless you do not wish to become a Buddha – if you wish to become a Buddha, you must have a male body; a female body cannot become a Buddha. To become a Bodhisattva you must also be male; a female body cannot become a Bodhisattva.

On hearing this, the cultivator believes, washing away his inherent mind, easily falling into deviant awakening.

Hearing the demon say such things and thinking: “He speaks truly – I always see Guanyin Bodhisattva depicted as a woman; that is conclusive proof.” Such people do not understand the Buddhadharma: Guanyin Bodhisattva is neither male nor female – responding according to beings' vows, teaching each according to their faculties. Her responsive manifestations are hard to distinguish – except by the demon king's spiritual powers, for the demon king also has powers and can transform itself. How can you tell who is a demon? Observe whether they harbor lust.

The original faith utterly vanishes – the true mind of cultivation originally there now wiped clean…

Easily falling into deviant understanding.

Sutra text: Thử danh mị quỷ, niên lão thành ma, não loạn thị nhân. Yểm túc tâm sanh, khứ bỉ nhân thể. Đệ tử dĩ sư, câu hãm vương nạn.

Translation: This is called a deluding ghost, aged into a demon, harassing this person. Sated, it arises and leaves that person's body. Both disciple and teacher fall into legal peril.

Commentary: This is called a deluding ghost – a demon among the li, mei, wang, liang kinds. Aged into a demon. It harasses the cultivator cultivating right samadhi. Sated, it leaves the possessed person's body. Both disciple and teacher fall into legal peril.

When the demon mind has tired of it, at last possessing people no more – both disciple and teacher fall into legal peril, both arrested and jailed.

Sutra text: Nhữ đương tiên giác, bất nhập luân hồi. Mê hoặc bất tri, đọa vô gián ngục.

Translation: You should be awakened beforehand, and not enter the turning wheel. Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

Commentary: You should be awakened at the very outset, lest you enter the demon king's wheel of birth and death – but lacking wisdom and deluded, unknowing what is happening, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

4 – GREED FOR KNOWLEDGE

Sutra text: Hựu thiện nam tử, thọ ấm hư diệu, bất tao tà lự, viên định phát minh. Tam-ma-địa  trung, tâm ái căn bản, cùng lãm vật hóa, tánh chi chung thủy. Tinh sảng kì tâm, tham cầu biện tích.

Translation: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed. Within samadhi the mind fond of origins, exhaustively surveying beings' transformations, natures from end to end – the mind keen and bright, greedily seeking analysis.

Commentary: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed.

Again, in the empty, penetrating, wondrous state after the feeling skandha has dissolved, the cultivator cultivating right samadhi no longer has deviant concerns, dwelling in the bright, perfect samadhi. Within samadhi the mind fond of knowing the origin of things: he decides: I shall study the physical origin of the universe.

Hence the cultivator exhaustively surveys the nature of things and their transformation from root to tip, to find what they ultimately are – making thought keen and sharp through greedily seeking analysis of things.

Sutra text: Nhĩ thời thiên ma, hậu đắc kì tiện, phi tinh phụ nhân, khẩu thuyết kinh pháp.

Translation: Then the heavenly demon gets its convenient chance, sending its essence to possess another person, using the possessed person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

Commentary: Then the heavenly demon gets its convenient chance –

Then the heavenly demon knows and says: “Aha! You have just given rise to a greedy mind – splendid! Now I can send my disciple to tempt you.” Thus it gets its convenient chance – again the demon king sends one of his followers, sending its essence to possess another person, using the possessed person's mouth to expound the demon king's Dharma.

Sutra text: Kì nhân tiên bất giác tri ma trước, diệc ngôn tự đắc, vô thượng niết bàn.  Lai bỉ cầu nguyên thiện nam tử xứ, phu tòa thuyết pháp. Thân hữu oai thần, tồi phục cầu giả, linh kì tòa hạ, tuy vị văn pháp, tự nhiên tâm phục. Thị chư nhân đẳng, tương Phật niết-bàn bồ-đề pháp thân, tức thị hiện tiền, ngã nhục thân thượng. Phụ phụ tử tử, đệ đại tương sanh, tức thị pháp thân thường trụ bất tuyệt. Đô chỉ hiện tại, tức vi Phật quốc, vô biệt tịnh cư, cập kim sắc tướng.

Translation: That person, first unaware of demonic possession, likewise claims to have attained unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the good man seeking origins, it spreads its seat and preaches the Dharma. Its body possessed of awesome spirit, subduing the seekers, so that beneath its seat, though not yet hearing the Dharma, they are naturally subdued in mind. It tells these people that the Buddha's nirvana, Bodhi, and Dharma-body are just the present fleshy body of self. Fathers and sons succeeding one another, generation after generation – this is the ever-abiding, unending Dharma-body. All points to the present: this very place is the Buddha-land; there is no separate Pure Abode, nor any golden-colored form.

Commentary: That person, unaware of being demon-possessed, likewise claims to have attained unsurpassed nirvana –

This is a case of the demon's stock line: “Everyone is a Buddha” – but a trick the heavenly demon often uses. This person truly does not know he is demon-possessed – having not a single notion of being possessed by the demon king, because he has grown deluded, all awareness lost when possessed: the demon takes total control, becoming the possessed person's announcer.

It claims to have attained the wondrous fruition of unsurpassed nirvana. When the demon comes to meet the one seeking to know the origin of things – seeking full knowledge of the physical phenomena of the universe – it spreads its seat, preaching the Dharma. Its (the demon king's) body possessed of awesome spirit, subduing the Dharma-seekers seeking the origin of all things. So that the assembly beneath its seat, though not yet hearing the Dharma, are naturally subdued in mind – their minds already subdued, deeply reverent.

It tells them the Buddha's Bodhi, nirvana, and Dharma-body are just the demon's present fleshy body: it says: “What are Bodhi and nirvana? They are right here, in this fleshy body of mine.”

It says fathers and sons succeeding one another, generation after generation, are the ever-abiding, unending Dharma-body.

Father begets son; son grows up becoming father, in turn begetting sons – the continuity of generations is ever-abiding, the ever-abiding, undying Dharma-body. What you see right now is precisely the Buddha-land; this very place right now is the Buddha-land. There is no separate Pure Abode, nor any golden-colored form.

There is no Pure Land to dwell in, nor any other golden form – all those are false. From its words, know clearly the mark of demons, the mark of ghosts. I often use the word demonic aura to speak of demons – this is what is called demonic aura: the demon's latent power possessing it, so everyone accepts whatever the demon lectures.

Sutra text: Kì nhân tín thọ, vong thất tiên tâm, thân mạng quy y, đắc vị tằng hữu. Thị đẳng ngu mê hoặc vi bồ-tát. Suy cứu kì tâm, phá Phật luật nghi, tiềm hành tham dục.

Translation: That person believes and accepts, losing the former mind – body and life taking refuge, gaining what never was. Such deluded ones mistake it for a Bodhisattva. Pursuing such fancies in mind, they break the Buddha's moral code, secretly practicing greed and lust.

Commentary: That person believes what the demon says, losing the original faith.

Hearing the demon say such things, the cultivator thinks: “So true – father begets son, son grows up as father, in turn begetting sons, generation succeeding generation – that is the ever-abiding, undying Dharma-body, always so since time without beginning.” The cultivator fully believes it.

Losing the original faith, the cultivator forgets right views – believing the demon more strongly than the right Dharma. When heavenly demons and outer paths tell him to do things, he dares not disobey; when a true good teacher teaches him to do good, he wavers between doubt and trust. The demon king harasses him with latent demonic power, so he believes whatever the demon says.

If you ask the demon king to lecture this Sutra (the Shurangama Sutra), it cannot lecture it: for the moment it speaks, its characteristic marks show. That is why I say, in America, if you ask anyone claiming mastery of Buddhist learning to lecture this Sutra, they will not dare – fearing exposure.

Giving body and life in refuge to the demon, feeling as gaining what never was: the cultivator deluded, deeming himself a Bodhisattva – truly pitiable, thinking the demon is a Bodhisattva. Pursuing such fancies, he studies with the demon, learning its magical arts. He no longer keeps the precepts; instead he breaks the Buddha's moral code, secretly practicing lustful acts – secretly abandoning himself to pleasure unknown to anyone.

Sutra text: Khẩu trung hảo ngôn nhãn nhĩ tỉ thiệt, giai vi tịnh độ. Nam nữ nhị căn, tức thị bồ-đề niết-bàn chân xứ. Bỉ vô tri giả, tín thị uế ngôn.

Translation: Its mouth delights in saying: eyes, ears, nose, tongue are all Pure Lands; the male and female organs are truly the place of Bodhi and nirvana. The ignorant believe such filthy words.

Commentary: This kind of demon king is truly vile! Its mouth delights in saying: eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, mind are all Pure Lands – you need seek the Pure Land Dharma-door nowhere else. It tells people: “That Dharma-door lies right in your own six organs.” It also says the male and female organs are truly Bodhi and nirvana – the seeds of Bodhi, the true abode of Bodhi and nirvana. Can you imagine such words?

The ignorant believe such filthy words: people lacking knowledge and wisdom hear this, saying: “Oh! Never before heard or seen anything like this – Bodhi and nirvana are just so.”

Despising their whole lives, they race down the road to death as life's most worthwhile deed, having believed such filthy, defiled words.

Sutra text: Thử danh cổ độc, yểm thắng ác quỷ, niên lão thành ma ,não loạn thị nhân. Yểm túc tâm sanh, khứ bỉ nhân thể. Đệ tử dữ sư, câu hãm vương nạn.

Translation: This is called gu-poison and oppressive evil ghosts, aged into demons, harassing this person. Sated, they arise and leave that person's body. Both disciple and teacher fall into legal peril.

Commentary: This is called gu-poison ghosts and oppressive ghosts, also called kumbhanda ghosts, aged into demons. They harass the cultivator cultivating right samadhi. But sated at last, they leave the possessed person's body, possessing people no more. Hence disciple and teacher both fall into legal peril – interfered with by the authorities, activities restricted, teacher and disciple both arrested and jailed.

Sutra text: Nhữ đương tiên giác, bất nhập luân hồi. Mê hoặc bất tri, đọa vô gián ngục

Translation: You should be awakened beforehand, and not enter the turning wheel. Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

Commentary: You should be awakened beforehand, and not enter the turning wheel. Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

You should awaken early, lest you enter the turning wheel – do not fall into the demon king's temptations. Deluded and unknowing, one is sure to fall into the uninterrupted hell.

5 – GREED FOR SECRET RESPONSE

Sutra text: Hựu thiện nam tử, thọ ấm hư diệu. bất tao tà lự, niên định phát minh, tam-ma-địa trung, tâm ái huyền ứng, chu lưu tinh nghiên, tham cầu minh cảm.

Translation: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed. Within samadhi the mind fond of mysterious response, thoroughly, pervasively investigating, greedily seeking secret resonance.

Commentary: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed.

Again, in the empty, penetrating, wondrous state after the feeling skandha has dissolved, the cultivator cultivating right samadhi no longer has deviant concerns, dwelling in the bright, perfect right samadhi.

At this point the cultivator can no longer be harmed by demons or outer paths. Within samadhi the mind suddenly longs to know matters before and after – mysterious matters occurring very far away. For example, you are in San Francisco wishing to know what is happening in New York: if you can know it, you have attained what is called “mysterious response” (knowing distant secret matters).

Hence thoroughly, pervasively investigating, greedily seeking secret resonance. Focusing all the mind's refined power in study, greedily seeking secret resonance.

He focuses all his strength studying this mysterious matter, longing for mysterious resonance: for instance, sitting in meditation in San Francisco, he can clearly see relatives and friends working in New York and clearly hear what they are saying. Later he discovers what he heard occurred exactly at that time. That is the kind of mysterious response he wishes to attain.

Sutra text: Nhĩ thời thiên ma, hậu đắc kì tiện, phi tinh phụ nhân, khẩu thuyết kinh pháp.

Translation: Then the heavenly demon, waiting for its convenient chance, sends its essence to possess another person, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

Commentary: Then the heavenly demon gets its convenient chance. At that time the heavenly demon notices the cultivator's samadhi power is about to be perfected and grows jealous. Gaining a convenient chance, it sends its descendants to watch for lapses – the moment it sees an opening, sending its essence to possess another person, using the possessed person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

Sutra text: Kì nhân nguyên bất giác tri ma trước, diệc ngôn tự đắc vô thượng niết-bàn. Lai bỉ cầu ứng thiện nam tử xứ, phu tòa thuyết pháp. Năng linh thính chúng, tạm kiến kì thân, như bách thiên tuế. Tâm sanh ái nhiễm, bất năng xả li. Thân vi nô bộc, tứ sự cúng dường, bất giác bì lao. Các các linh kì, tòa hạ nhân tâm, tri thị tiên sư, bổn thiện tri thức, biệt sanh pháp ái, niêm như giao tất, đắc vị tằng hữu.

Translation: That person, originally unaware of demonic possession, likewise claims to have attained unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the good man seeking response, it spreads its seat and preaches the Dharma – able to make its listeners briefly see its body as a hundred thousand years old. Their minds giving rise to fond defilement, unable to leave it; their bodies serving as servants, offering the four requisites without ever tiring. Each beneath its seat is made to know in mind: this is my former teacher, my original good friend – giving rise to a special love for the Dharma, sticking like glue and lacquer, gaining what never was.

Commentary: That person, originally unaware of being possessed, likewise claiming to have realized unsurpassed nirvana. The demon comes to the place of the one seeking mysterious response, spreading its seat, preaching the Dharma.

The good man possessed by the demon, in a moment, making its listeners see its body as a hundred thousand years old.

You should know that perception is momentary: when someone in the assembly sees him with the gray-haired head of an old man upon a child's body, they think him a veteran cultivator, an elder bhikshu.

Their minds giving rise to fond defilement, unable to leave him: this impure fondness – entanglement and defilement – once arisen as love, brings turbidity; with defilement, purity is lost.

All who come to hear the demon lecture want to follow it day and night. Why? They are enchanted by its particular attraction. Their bodies serving as servants, offering it the four requisites without ever tiring.

The four offerings are: 1. food and drink, 2. clothing, 3. bedding and sitting gear, 4. medicines. They never feel bored or weary offering these things to the demon. Some wonder why they act so: a genuine cultivator, a true disciple of the Buddha, would never draw near and make offerings so. Only because the heavenly demon has a particular attractive, enchanting power making everyone like to stay near it.

The assembly beneath the Dharma seat believes that person (the demon) is their teacher from a past life: it creates such confusion that everyone believes the possessed person is their good friend from a past life, thinking: “He was my teacher in a past life.”

They give rise to a special love for their Dharma master, sticking to him like glue and lacquer, feeling as gaining what never was – thinking: never before was it so.

Sutra text: Thị nhân ngu mê, hoặc vi bồ-tát. Thân cận kì tâm phá Phật luật nghi, tiềm hành  tham dục.

Translation: That person, deluded, mistakes it for a Bodhisattva; drawing near its mind, breaking the Buddha's moral code, secretly practicing greed and lust.

Commentary: That person, deluded to the extreme, deeming it one able to transform itself, hence surely a Buddha or a Bodhisattva. Fox-spirits and other kinds of demons and ghosts can all transform. But he cannot think through that one skillful in transformation is not necessarily a Bodhisattva or a Buddha. What good roots have you planted that you now expect to meet Buddhas and Bodhisattvas?

Drawing near the demon's mind: the person draws near the demon-possessed one. Breaking the Buddha's moral code: this is a most important point – how do we know the person is a demon? We can state at once: it has broken the Buddha's precepts – and secretly practices lustful acts.

Sutra text: Khẩu trung hảo ngôn, ngã ư tiền thế, ư mỗ sanh trung, tiên độ mỗ nhân, đương thời thị ngã, thê thiếp huynh đệ,  kim lai tương độ, dữ nhữ tương tùy, quy mỗ thế giới, cúng dường mỗ Phật. Hoặc ngôn biệt hữu, đại quang minh thiên, Phật ư trung trụ,nhất thiết Như Lai, sở hưu cư địa. Bỉ vô tri giả, tín  thị hư cuống, di thất bản tâm.

Translation: Its mouth delights in saying: “In a past life, in such a life, I already saved such a person – then my wife, concubines, brothers – now come again to save one another; I shall go with you to follow one another to such a world, to make offerings to such a Buddha.” Or saying there is apart a Great Bright Light Heaven where Buddhas dwell – the resting dwelling of all Tathagatas. The unknowing believe such empty lies, losing their inherent minds.

Commentary: Whenever meeting someone, the demon delights in saying: “In a past life I already saved such a person – then my wife, or my brother – now come again to save one another –

Like the story of Liu Jin-tong I told before: she often told her victims they had been her children in a past life and her husbands in another past life. Now this one says:

“In a past life, in such a life – sometimes in the hundred-and-first or hundred-and-second life –

I already saved such a person – then my wife or my brother.” So it speaks. “Now I come to save one another; I shall go with you inseparably. I shall go with you to follow one another to such a world, to make offerings to such a Buddha.

Or it says: “There is a Great Bright Light Heaven – we shall go there.” In fact the heaven it mentions is where the demon king dwells. It says: that is where the Buddhas and Tathagatas rest. That is where the Buddha of this life – all present Buddhas you believe in are false – and the Tathagatas rest within. When the Buddhas tire of teaching beings in the world, they return to the Great Bright Light Heaven to rest.”

When the unknowing believe such deceitful words, the result is they lose their inherent minds, their original faith.

Sutra text: Thử danh lệ quỷ, niên lão thành ma, não loạn thị nhân. Yểm túc tâm sanh, khứ bỉ nhân thể. Đệ tử dữ sư câu hãm vương nạn.

Translation: This is called a pestilence-ghost, aged into a demon, harassing the cultivator. Sated, no longer possessing that person. Both teacher and disciple fall into legal peril.

Commentary: This is a kind of pestilence-ghost, after more than three to five thousand years, aged into a demon. It harasses, torments the cultivator, striving to destroy the cultivator's samadhi power. But after a time, when it has played all its cheating tricks and the games hold nothing new – sated, no longer possessing that person. Then both teacher and disciple fall into legal peril.

Once the heavenly demon leaves that person's body, it no longer has its alluring demonic power, so people begin to doubt it – at last it is sued and jailed.

Sutra text: Nhữ đương tiên giác, bất nhập luân hồi. Mê hoặc bất tri, đọa vô gián ngục.

Translation: You should be awakened beforehand, and not enter the turning wheel. Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

Commentary: You should know these matters beforehand – early awaken to this principle – lest you enter the turning wheel; do not fall into the demon's tempting net, do not enter the demon king's turning wheel of birth and death. Deluded, unknowing this principle, one is sure to fall into the uninterrupted hell.

6 – GREED FOR STILLNESS

Sutra text: Hựu thiện nam tử, thọ ấm  hư diệu, bất tao tà lự, viên định phát minh. Tam-ma-địa  trung, tâm ái thâm nhập, khắc kỉ tân cần, nhạo xứ âm tịch, tham cầu tĩnh mật.

Translation: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed. Within samadhi the mind fond of deep entering, restraining the self in diligence, delighting in dwelling in gloom and quiet, greedily seeking still seclusion.

Commentary: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns,

Again, in the empty, penetrating, wondrous state after the feeling skandha has dissolved, the cultivator cultivating right samadhi no longer has deviant concerns – the perfect samadhi disclosed, dwelling in the bright, perfect samadhi. Within samadhi the mind gives rise to longing, fond of deeply entering diligent, austere effort, delighting in dwelling in gloom and quiet.

The cultivator restrains himself very tightly, putting all strength into effort – fond of dwelling where yin energy abounds with little sunlight, fond of unfrequented places like caves, deep mountains, or remote valleys, choosing a place to live in seclusion. Because he overly craves stillness, the demon king comes.

In cultivation effort, one should not crave excessively: crave neither good things nor bad – the ordinary mind is the Way. Mainly keep the mind ordinary, giving rise to not a single thought. Whatever you greedily seek is wrong.

Sutra text: Nhĩ thời thiên ma, hậu đắc kì tiện. Phi tinh phụ nhân, khẩu thuyết kinh pháp.

Translation: Then the heavenly demon gets its chance, sending its essence to possess another person, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

Commentary: This state is like the previous case. Then the heavenly demon gets its chance – when the convenient moment comes. At once sending its essence to possess another person, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma: the demon sends its disciple to possess someone else, then makes that person go to where the craving cultivator is, to expound sutras and Dharma.

Sutra text: Kì nhân bổn bất giác tri ma trước, diệc ngôn tự đắc vô thượng niết-bàn. Lai bỉ cầu âm thiện nam tử xứ, phu tòa thuyết pháp. Linh kì thính nhân, các tri bản nghiệp. Hoặc ư kì xứ, ngữ nhất nhân ngôn. Nhữ kim vị tử, dĩ tác súc sanh. Sắc sử nhất  nhân, ư hậu đạp vĩ, đốn linh kì nhân, khởi bất năng đắc. Ư thị nhất chúng, khuynh tâm khâm phục. Hữu nhân khởi tâm, dĩ tri kì triệu. Phật luật nghi ngoại, trùng gia tinh khổ. Phỉ báng tỷ-khưu, mạ lị đồ chúng, kiết lộ nhân sự, bất tị cơ hiềm. Khẩu trung hảo ngôn, vị nhiên họa phúc, cập chí kì thời, hào bị vô thất.

Translation: That person, originally unaware of demonic possession, likewise claims to have attained unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the good man seeking seclusion, it spreads its seat and preaches the Dharma – making its listeners each know their past karma. Or in that place, telling one person: “Though not yet dead, you have already become an animal;” ordering a person behind to step on his tail, at once making that person unable to rise. Thereupon the whole assembly bows in admiration. If anyone gives rise to a thought, it already knows the omen. Beyond the Buddha's moral code, it redoubles ascetic rigor – slandering bhikshus, scolding its followers, exposing people's affairs, heedless of ridicule and suspicion. Its mouth delights in foretelling coming fortune and calamity, and when the time arrives, not a hair off.

Commentary: That person, originally unaware of being demon-possessed. He proclaims as the demon king says – having attained unsurpassed nirvana.

What evidence judges someone a demon king? In that demons almost invariably love praising themselves.

It says: “Do you know? I have just realized nirvana” – or it may say: “I have just realized the first Arhat fruition” – or: “I have attained the fourth Arhat fruition” – or “I have now become a Bodhisattva – do you recognize it?”

The moment someone proclaims so, you know at once he is a demon, no need to ask. The Buddha never says:

“I am a Buddha – quickly come bow to me. If you do not bow to me, you have missed a great chance, for I am a Buddha – how stupid not to bow to me.”

Whoever proclaims himself a Buddha, a Bodhisattva, an Arhat is a demon and nothing else – you can know at once, no need to ask. Those are demons' words. A Buddha never claims to be a Buddha; a Bodhisattva manifesting in the world never styles himself a Bodhisattva. Even when someone honors them as Bodhisattvas, they do not acknowledge it.

Even if the person is a Buddha and someone says: “I know you are a Buddha,” they do not acknowledge it either. One truly awakened never admits to others his awakening. If someone says “I am awakened,” pay him no mind – he is not worth comparing even to an animal. Do not listen to such boasting self-praise.

Hearing sutra lectures equips you with a demon-revealing mirror: once demons, ghosts, and goblins show their forms, you know them at once. But if you do not clearly understand the Buddhadharma, you will not know what they say and will at once be fooled by them.

Coming to the cultivator seeking still seclusion, spreading its seat, preaching the Dharma.

When he (the possessed person) comes to the cultivator seeking still seclusion, it spreads its seat, preaching the Dharma. (24), (25). It makes all listeners clearly know their past-life karma.

Everyone feels as if knowing clearly in a dream what they were, who they were, in a past life. Some say: “In a distant eon I was a watchdog.” Some say: “I was a cat.” Others say: “I was a chicken.” Still others say: “In a past life I was an ox.” No one was a person.

Or it (the demon king) tells someone there: “Though not yet dead, you have already become an animal.” What does it mean? This: “You were a dog in a past life – now, though not yet dead, you have turned into a dog again. Do you not believe me?” Then telling someone behind to step on the tail of the one in front: it tells everyone: “He does not believe what I say – go behind him and step on his tail and see if he can rise.”

Then it stamps its foot hard on the ground, saying it is stepping on the tail of the one in front. Suddenly that person cannot rise – surely you would think he really has spiritual powers. After the demon says that person has a tail, then tells another to step on it, and the person cannot rise – the person has no choice but to believe it: “He says I am an animal – now I truly have a tail; if not, why, when someone steps on my tail behind, can I not rise?”

Thereupon the whole assembly bows in admiration.

“How miraculous!” they say. “He knew beforehand that person would turn into an animal while still alive – he must be a living Buddha or Bodhisattva.” In fact they have been fooled by the demon without knowing it – meeting a ghost or demon king yet mistaking it for a Bodhisattva: truly the upside-downness of beings.

If anyone gives rise to a doubting thought, the demon at once knows the intention.

If in the assembly someone doubts, thinking: “How can that be? Truly unreasonable” – the moment the doubting thought arises, the demon knows and replies: “So you do not believe me?” These people look back at it a moment and say: “Oh! He truly is a Bodhisattva – I never spoke what I thought, yet he knows it clearly, exposing all my doubts. How strange!” From then on he dares show no disbelief.

Beyond the Buddha's moral code, it redoubles ascetic rigor.

It says: “The Buddha's moral code is not enough for me – I shall establish a new code for you. I want you to become new Buddhas, and I shall found a new Buddhism: present-day Buddhism is too outdated, no longer fitting. Now is the age of science, the nuclear age – everything must be modernized and improved; old ways of thinking are no longer useful; that ancient Buddhism has no more application.”

That is how it transforms Buddhism – saying everyone can turn into venerable elders, bhikshus, or anyone they wish.

It slanders bhikshus.

It says: Bhikshus! What are bhikshus? It plays with the name, saying: “You call him a bhikshu? I call that a loach” – in Chinese, the word bhikshu and ni-qiu 泥 鰍 (loach) sound alike at the end.

It scolds its followers, exposing people's affairs.

It reviles and scolds its followers whenever it pleases, calling them: “You are dogs, cats, pigs, rabbits…” The followers hear its scolding, accepting such abuse, thinking it a Bodhisattva: “He says I am a pig – then a pig I am; he says I am a dog – then a dog I am.” They dare not argue back. The demon king has a fierce power enchanting everyone, making everyone believe whatever it says.

It exposes people's affairs: for instance, a man and woman doing something slightly improper – it tells the woman: “You did that thing with that man at that place.” The woman thinks: “How does he know?” Or it exposes before the public: “Here are two scoundrels – they did improper things, things inconvenient to speak of, at that place and that. Ask her about it – she will not dare deny!” It wants to bring up what they actually did, so they dare not deny. It does so to prove to everyone: it has spiritual powers, knowing even things about to happen. It exposes people's private faults, heedless of ridicule or suspicion – revealing each personal secret, fearing no contempt.

Its mouth delights in foretelling coming fortune and calamity, and when the time arrives, not a hair off.

It loves predicting fortune and calamity – loves saying things like: “Be careful – tomorrow is a bad day for you; someone wants to poison you – examine your food closely, or you will die of poison.”

It loves foretelling both good and bad beforehand. When the matter occurs, indeed not a hair off: when the event occurs, it exactly matches its prediction. That is why everyone believes it – such a demon king makes people believe more readily than a Bodhisattva.

Sutra text: Thử đại lực quỷ, niên lão thành ma, não loạn thị nhân. Yếm túc tâm sanh, khứ bỉ nhân thể. Đệ tử dữ sư, đa hãm vương nạn. Nhữ đương tiên giác, bất nhập luân hồi. Mê hoặc bất tri, đọa vô gián ngục.

Translation: This is a mighty-power ghost, aged long into a demon, harassing this person. Sated, it arises and leaves that person's body. Teacher and disciple mostly fall into legal peril. You should be awakened beforehand, and not enter the turning wheel. Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

Commentary: This is a mighty-power ghost, a demon grown old – demons turning into ghosts in old age. Just as people who do not cultivate, planting virtuous causes, in old age turn into sprites – as I often tell you. The Chinese have a saying: “Old yet undying makes a villain – growing old without dying is villainy.”

When people live long and pass through many experiences, they often do bizarre things; likewise, long a demon, it turns into a ghost.

It harasses the cultivator – jealous of the cultivator's effort, demons love destroying the cultivator's samadhi power.

Sated, it leaves the possessed person's body. Then both teacher and disciple fall into legal peril – likewise tantamount to falling into the hells. Hence the saying:

The ignorant transmitting to the ignorant,
One transmission, both ignorant;
The master descends into hell,
The disciples crowd in after.

Free translation:
The ignorant teaching the ignorant,
The more learned, the more benighted;
The master falls into hell,
The disciples follow at his heels.

These words accord with the Sutra's principle: meeting no enlightened teacher, the disciple also of dull faculties – when seeing the master enter hell, he follows his master right in. The master turns and asks: “What are you doing here?”

The disciple answers: “Seeing my master enter here, of course I must follow.”

The master says: “Oh! You should not. This is no peaceful place. You should never have come!”

The disciple replies:

– “But my master entered first! How could I not follow? I studied with my master – where my master goes, I follow.”

The master thinks: “Ah! I myself fell into hell, dragging my disciples in with me. I truly wronged you. Alas!”

You should know these matters beforehand, lest you enter the turning wheel. Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

7 – GREED FOR KNOWLEDGE OF PAST LIVES

Sutra text: Hựu thiện nam tử, thọ ấm  hư diệu, bất tao tà lự, viên định phát minh. Tam-ma-địa  trung, tâm ái tri kiến, cần khổ nghiên tầm, tham cầu túc mạng.

Translation: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed. Within samadhi the mind fond of much knowledge – diligently, bitterly investigating, greedily seeking past lives.

Commentary: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed. In the empty, penetrating, wondrous state after the feeling skandha has dissolved, the cultivator no longer has deviant concerns, dwelling in the bright, perfect samadhi. Within samadhi the mind fond of gaining more knowledge.

In samadhi the cultivator craves to understand more matters, longing for understanding of lives in past eons – putting forth all effort, fearing no hardship.

Hence diligently, bitterly investigating, longing to know lives in past eons.

Sutra text: Nhĩ thời thiên ma, hậu đắc cầu tiện, phi tinh phụ nhân, khẩu thuyết kinh pháp. Kì nhân thù bất giác tri ma trước, diệc ngôn tự đắc vô thượng niết-bàn.  Lai bỉ cầu tri thiện nam tử xứ, phu tòa thuyết pháp.

Translation: Then the heavenly demon gets its sought chance, sending its essence to possess that person's body, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma. That person, wholly unaware of demonic possession, likewise claims to have realized unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the good man seeking knowledge, it spreads its seat and preaches the Dharma.

Commentary: Then the heavenly demon gets its convenient chance, sending its essence to possess another's body, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma. That person, unaware of being demon-possessed – wholly unaware his body has been seized and commanded by demons.

Likewise claiming to have realized unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the good man seeking knowledge, spreading its seat, preaching the Dharma.

Sutra text: Thị nhân vô đoan, ư thuyết pháp xứ, đắc đại bảo châu. Kì ma hoặc thời, hóa vi súc sanh,  khẩu hàm kì châu, cập tạp trân bảo, giản sách  phù độc, chư kì dị vật. Tiên thụ bỉ nhân, trước kỳ thể. Hoặc dụ thính nhân, tàng ư địa hạ. hữu minh nguyệt châu, chiếu diệu kỳ xứ. Thị chư thính giả, đắc vị tằng hữu. Đa thực  dược  thảo,  bất xan gia thiện. Hoặc thời nhật xan, nhất ma nhất mạch, kỳ hình phì sung, quỷ lực trì cố. Phỉ báng tỳ-khưu, mạ lị đồ chúng, bất tị kị hiềm.

Translation: That person, for no reason, at the Dharma-preaching place obtains a great precious pearl. At times the demon transforms into an animal, its mouth holding that pearl, along with assorted jewels, bamboo tallies, talismans, and sundry strange things – first presenting them to that person, then possessing his body. Or it deludes its listeners by burying something underground, saying: there is a moon-bright pearl illuminating that place – so its listeners feel they gain what never was. It mostly eats medicinal herbs, not fine prepared food; or at times eats but a sesame seed, a wheat grain a day, its form plump and full, upheld by ghost power. Slandering bhikshus, scolding its followers, heedless of ridicule and suspicion.

Commentary: At the Dharma assembly, that person suddenly as if obtains a great precious pearl – perhaps a diamond or a wish-fulfilling pearl.

At times the demon transforms into an animal, its mouth holding jewels, bamboo tallies, talismans, and other strange things, claiming Bodhisattvas can transform their bodies into anything – the animal-mouth the demon has transformed holding jewels, bamboo tallies, talismans.

Bamboo tallies (jian-ce) were used for records in ancient times: characters written on one face, then the bamboo slip split in two, the writing showing on each face's surface. When these tallies were needed as credentials, the two halves were joined: matching meant the tally counted as a credential; non-matching halves meant untrustworthy.

Talismans are used to subdue and seize demons, ghosts, and goblins – and the animal the demon transforms into may carry other strange things, all bizarre, rare, and very valuable.

First presenting them to that person, then possessing his body.

Or the demon deludes the Dharma-listeners by burying something underground, saying: there is a “bright pearl” shining there.

It buries the pearl underground, fooling the Dharma-listeners, saying: “Beneath here is a bright pearl, its light like the moon shedding light here.”

So its listeners all feel they gain what never was.

They marvel: “Oh! This person is genuine – he cannot possibly be a demon!”

He is squarely a demon, yet they insist he is not. Pity those who come to hear it lecture.

The demon usually eats only medicinal herbs, not prepared food.

It usually eats only medicinal herbs, not ordinary food – no fine food: it takes ginseng and some tonics.

When I was in Hong Kong, I met a person claiming never to eat ordinary food – he served as a spirit-medium for those praying for long life, sons, wealth, and other things. Whenever at someone else's home, he announced he ate no ordinary food. What then did he eat? Walnuts – walnut kernels containing much oil, very nourishing for the brain – a little suffices for the body to function. If one usually eats a bowl of rice, half a bowl of walnuts suffices. Or it also eats pine kernels – in short, only the most nourishing things.

Or it eats but a sesame seed, a wheat grain a day, yet looks hale – fatter than a pig. Upheld by ghost power. (27)

It slanders bhikshus and scolds its followers, heedless of ridicule and suspicion.

It specializes in reviling Sangha Masters, the left-home ones: “Left-home people? What did they leave home for? They cultivate nothing – do left-home people not crave money? With them, the more the better!”

Or it says: “Why do you believe them? They are only people, too – you are utter fools in the end.”

When someone believes the bhikshus, it calls them “fools,” scolding its own followers as animals and such vile things, wholly heedless of slanderous words.

Sutra text: Khẩu trung hảo ngôn, tha phương bảo tạng, thập phương thánh hiền, tiềm nặc chi xứ. Tùy kỳ hậu giả, vãng vãng kiến hữu, kì dị chi nhân.

Translation: Its mouth delights in speaking of treasuries in distant places, or the hidden dwelling of holy sages of the ten directions. Those following it often see strange and unusual people.

Commentary: It delights in speaking of treasuries in strange lands: what does it love to speak of? It says: “Over there, in that place, are gold, silver, and jewels – do you want to get them?” It spreads such rumors to enchant people; or it loves speaking of the hidden dwelling of holy sages of the ten directions, telling people: “Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are cultivating in that place, wholly unknown to you.”

Those following it often see strange and unusual people – it can emit light or display very strange features.

Sutra text: Thử danh sơn lâm, thổ địa thành hoàng, xuyên nhạc quỷ thần, niên lão thành ma. Hoặc hữu tuyên dâm, phá Phật giới luật, dữ thừa sự giả, tiềm hành ngũ dục; hoặc hữu tinh tiến, thuần thực thảo mộc, vô định hành sự, não loạn bỉ nhân. Yếm túc tâm sanh, khứ bỉ nhân thể. Đệ tử dữ sư, đa hãm vương nạn.

Translation: This is called a demon – mountain and forest spirits, earth, city-gods, river and mountain ghosts and spirits, aged into ghosts. The possessed person advocates lust, breaking the Buddha's moral code – secretly practicing the five desires with its attendants; or else vigorously eating only herbs, acting without samadhi, harassing that person. Sated, it arises and leaves that person's body. Disciple and teacher mostly fall into legal peril.

Commentary: What kind of being is this? This is a kind of demon – mountain and forest spirits, earth, city-gods, river and mountain, aged over a long time into ghosts. The possessed person advocates lust, breaking the Buddha's moral code: lustful thoughts make it break the precepts. It secretly practices lust with its disciples who likewise enjoy the five desires: wealth, beauty, fame, food, sleep.

Or else it vigorously eats only herbs, acting erratically. It does not sit in meditation or apply any cultivation effort – only following useless asceticism.

Harassing the cultivator, making them unable to cultivate the Way anymore.

But after a time, sated, it no longer possesses people; teacher and disciple both fall into legal peril.

Sutra text: Nhữ đương tiên giác, bất nhập luân hồi. Mê hoặc bất tri, đọa vô gián ngục.

Translation: You should be awakened beforehand, and not enter the turning wheel. Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

Commentary: You should know this matter beforehand, lest you enter the turning wheel.

Awaken early to this situation, lest you enter the demon's trap – do not enter the demon-spread net of the turning wheel of birth and death.

Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

8 – GREED FOR SPIRITUAL POWERS

Sutra text: Hựu thiện nam tử,  thọ ấm hư diệu, bất tao tà lự, viên định phát minh. Tam-ma-địa trung, tâm ái thần thông, chủng chủng biến hóa. Nghiên cứu hóa nguyên, tham thủ thần lực.

Translation: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed. Within samadhi the mind fond of spiritual powers and all transformations – studying the origin of transformations, greedily seeking spiritual powers.

Commentary: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, in the empty, penetrating, wondrous state after the feeling skandha has dissolved, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed. Within samadhi the mind fond of spiritual powers. He has another false thought – determined to gain spiritual powers and all transforming abilities, to display the eighteen transformations in the air: water shooting from the upper body, fire issuing from the lower body; fire from above, water from below. He burns to be like the Arhats, displaying these eighteen spiritual transformations floating in the air.

Hence studying the origin of such transformations, studying the fundamental source of transforming powers, greedily seeking spiritual powers.

Sutra text: Nhĩ thời thiên ma, hậu đắc kì tiện, phi tinh phụ nhân, khẩu thuyết kinh pháp.

Translation: Then the heavenly demon gets its convenient chance, sending its essence to possess another person, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

Commentary: Then the heavenly demon gets its convenient chance, sending its essence to possess another person, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

The heavenly demon, long awaiting a convenient chance, at once sends its essence to possess another person, then commands that person to lecture Sutras and Dharma.

Sutra text: Kì nhân thành bất giác tri ma trước. Diệc ngôn tự đắc vô thượng niết-bàn. Lai bỉ cầu thông thiện nam tử xứ, phu tòa thuyết pháp. Thị nhân hoặc phục, thủ chấp hỏa quang, thủ toát kì quang, phân ư sở thính, tứ chúng đầu thượng, thị chư thính nhân,đỉnh thượng hỏa quang, giai trưởng sổ xích, diệc vô nhiệt tánh, tằng bất phần thiêu. Hoặc thượng thủy hành, như lí bình địa, hoặc ư không trung, an tọa bất động, hoặc nhập bình nội, hoặc xử nang trung, việt dũ thấu viên, tằng vô chướng ngại. Duy ư đao binh, bất đắc tự tại. Tự ngôn thị Phật, thân trước bạch y, thọ tỉ khưu lễ, phỉ báng thiền luật, mạ lị đồ chúng, yết lộ nhân sự, bất tị cơ hiềm.

Translation: That person, truly unaware of demonic possession, likewise claims to have attained unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the good man seeking powers, it spreads its seat and preaches the Dharma. That person may grasp firelight in hand, gathering the light and scattering it over the heads of the fourfold assembly listening – the firelight atop each listener's crown several feet high, yet neither hot nor ever burning. Or walking on water as on level ground; or sitting unmoving in the air; or entering into a jar or a bag; or passing through windows, through walls, without obstruction. Only with weapons it is not at ease. Claiming to be a Buddha, its body clad in white, receiving bhikshus' homage – slandering Chan and the Vinaya, scolding its followers, exposing people's affairs, heedless of ridicule and suspicion.

Commentary: That person, unaware of demonic possession, likewise claiming to have attained the wondrous fruition of unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the good man seeking spiritual powers, spreading its seat, preaching the Dharma.

That person may grasp firelight in hand – grasping fire in one hand – gathering the light with the other hand, then scattering the fire over the heads of the fourfold assembly listening: placing fire on each listener's head one by one. The firelight atop their heads several feet high: placed on the head small at first, then the fire grows gradually to several feet. Yet neither hot nor burning – though using nothing to shield from the fire.

Or it (the possessed person) can walk on water as on level ground, or sit unmoving in the air – nothing holding him floating in the air, yet he can sit still upon it…

Or enter into a jar or a bag, or pass through windows, through walls, without obstruction: doors and windows shut, yet it passes through with ease, unopened, without the least obstruction.

Only with weapons it is not at ease: it fears being stabbed by knives, spears, swords – for it still has a material body obstructing. Though possessing five kinds of spiritual powers, it still fears injury from weapons.

Claiming to have become a Buddha, yet clad in lay white – not wearing the left-home robes.

Receiving bhikshus' homage: clad as a layperson, yet accepting bhikshus' homage. Slandering Chan samadhi and the Vinaya – deeming them useless and unreasonable.

Scolding its disciples and exposing people's faults: exposing people's private faults. Heedless of ridicule and suspicion.

Sutra text: Khẩu trung thường thuyết, thần thông tự tại, hoặc phục linh nhân, bàng kiến Phật độ.  Quỷ lực cảm nhân, phi hữu chân thực. Tán thán hành dâm, bất hủy thô hạnh. Tương chư ổi tá, dĩ vi truyền pháp.

Translation: Its mouth constantly speaks of spiritual powers and self-mastery, or else making people see Buddha-lands nearby. Moved by ghost power, nothing truly real. Praising lustful conduct, not renouncing coarse acts – taking all defiled conduct as transmitting the Dharma.

Commentary: It constantly speaks of the various kinds of spiritual powers and self-mastery, or else making people see Buddha-lands pervading the ten directions. Those lands are unreal, only appearing through demonic power to delude people: in fact it has no real skill-power at all – what it praises most is lust, saying: “That is truly the most marvelous – the source of Bodhi and nirvana.” It does not renounce coarse acts, saying: “Nothing is wrong with that – do not bother keeping precepts.”

Taking all defiled conduct as transmitting the Dharma. It uses every defiled deed as a means of transmitting the Dharma.

Sutra text: Thử danh thiên địa, đại lực sơn tinh, hải tinh phong tinh, hà tinh thổ tinh, nhất thiết thảo mộc, tích kiếp tinh mị. Hoặc phục long mị, hoặc thọ chung tiên, tái hoạt vi mị. Hoặc tiên kì chung, kế niên ưng tử, kì hình bất hóa, tha quái sở phụ. Niên lão thành ma, não loạn thị nhân. Yếm túc tâm sanh, khứ bỉ nhân thể. Đệ tử dữ sư, đa hãm vương nạn.

Translation: This is called the mighty spirits of heaven and earth – mountain sprites, sea sprites, wind sprites, river sprites, earth sprites, and the essences of all plants and trees accumulated over eons; or dragon-goblins; or immortals whose lifespan ended, revived as goblins; or immortals whose retribution ended and who should have died, yet whose forms do not decay, possessed by other goblins. Aged long into demons, harassing this person. Sated, they arise and leave that person's body. Disciple and teacher mostly fall into legal peril.

Commentary: This is called the mighty spirits of heaven and earth – mountain sprites, sea sprites, wind sprites, river sprites, earth sprites, and the accumulated-eon essences of all plants and trees. Or dragon-goblins (dragon-demons); or immortals whose lifespan ended, revived as goblins – sometimes a thousand, two, three, or up to five thousand years old, lifespan ended, revived as goblins. Or immortals whose retribution ended and who should have died, yet whose forms after death do not decay or change, hence possessed by other goblins.

These kinds, long-lived, turn into ghosts, harassing the samadhi power of cultivators. At last, sated, no longer possessing people.

While the demon still possesses the body, the possessed person has extraordinary samadhi power. But once it possesses no more, both disciple and teacher fall into legal peril.

Sutra text: Nhữ đương tiên giác bất nhập luân hồi. Mê hoặc bất tri đọa vô gián ngục

Translation: You should be awakened beforehand, and not enter the turning wheel. Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

Commentary: Ananda, you should know this matter beforehand, lest you enter the demon king's turning wheel – do not fall into the demon king's temptations.

Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

9 – GREED FOR PROFOUND EMPTINESS (THE DEMON OF SUNK EMPTINESS)

Sutra text: Hựu thiện nam tử,  thọ ấm  hư diệu, bất tao tà lự, viên định phát minh. Tam-ma-địa  trung, tâm ái nhập diệt, nghiên cứu hóa tánh, tham cầu thâm không.

Translation: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed. Within samadhi the mind fond of entering extinction, studying the nature of transformation, greedily seeking profound emptiness.

Commentary: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed. In the empty, penetrating, wondrous state after the feeling skandha has dissolved, the cultivator no longer has deviant concerns, dwelling in the bright, perfect samadhi. Within samadhi the mind fond of entering extinction, studying the nature of transformation, greedily seeking profound emptiness.

The cultivator studies how a body transforms from existence to nothingness, and how from nothingness it transforms back to existence – studying the manifestation of this transformation, longing to experience a wondrous, empty state.

Sutra text: Nhĩ thời thiên ma hậu đắc kì tiện, phi tinh phụ nhân, khẩu thuyết kinh pháp.

Translation: Then the heavenly demon gets its convenient chance, sending its essence flying to possess another person, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

Commentary: Then the heavenly demon gets a convenient chance – the heavenly demon watching for when it sees a convenient chance – at once sending its essence flying to possess another person, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

The demon lectures the Dharma through the mouth of the person it has possessed.

Sutra text: Kì nhân chung bất giác tri ma trước, diệc ngôn tự đắc vô thượng niết-bàn. Lai bỉ cầu không thiện nam tử xứ, phu tòa thuyết pháp. Ư đại chúng nội, kì hình hốt không, chúng vô sở kiến, hoàn tùng hư không, đột nhiên nhi xuất, tồn một tự tại. Hoặc hiện kì thân, đỗng như lưu li, hoặc thuỳ thủ túc, tác chiên đàn khí, hoặc đại tiểu tiện, như hậu thạch mật. Phỉ huỷ giới luật, khinh tiện xuất gia.

Translation: That person, never aware of demonic possession, likewise claims to have attained unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the good man seeking emptiness, it spreads its seat and preaches the Dharma. Amid the great assembly, its form suddenly becomes empty – none see it – then from empty space suddenly emerging, existing and vanishing at will. Or manifesting its body transparent as crystal; or stretching its limbs, emitting sandalwood fragrance; or excrement and urine like rock candy. Slandering the moral code, slighting the left-home.

Commentary: That person, never aware of being demon-possessed, likewise claiming to have attained unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the one seeking empty stillness – coming to the good man craving spiritual powers – spreading its seat, preaching the Dharma.

Amid the great assembly, its form suddenly becomes empty – none see it.

Demonic power makes the possessed person's body suddenly vanish – seated there preaching the Dharma, suddenly no one sees it anymore. This is a kind of “people empty, dharmas empty.” People and dharmas both empty. Then from empty space suddenly emerging, existing and vanishing at will.

Then minutes later, demonic power making the possessed person's body suddenly vanish – seated there preaching the Dharma, suddenly it reappears: appearing and vanishing at will – appearing if it wishes to appear, vanishing if it wishes to vanish, all controlled at its will.

Or manifesting its body transparent as crystal – so crystalline you can see right through its body. Stretching its limbs, emitting sandalwood fragrance. Or excrement and urine like rock candy. It slanders the moral code, saying: “Do not bother keeping the precepts – that is Small Vehicle business; why should you keep them? The precepts matter nothing at all.”

Slighting the left-home: it says: “No need to leave home. If you wish to cultivate, just cultivate – why must you leave home to cultivate? What difference between laypeople and the left-home?” That is how it slights the left-home estate.

Sutra text: Khẩu trung thường thuyết vô nhân vô quả. Nhất tử vĩnh diệt, vô phục hậu thân, cập chư phàm thánh, tuy đắc không tịch, tiềm hành tham dục. Thọ kì dục giả, diệc đắc không tâm, bát vô cause and effect.

Translation: Its mouth constantly says there is no cause and no effect: at death eternally extinguished, no further body after, nor any ordinary or holy – though having attained empty stillness, secretly practicing greed and lust. Those receiving its lust likewise gain the empty mind, denying cause and effect.

Commentary: It constantly says there is no cause and effect – “Do not believe in the law of cause and effect,” it says: “That is utterly mistaken – never any such thing.” It says: at death eternally extinguished – “Once dead, one never returns – like a lamp utterly gone out.”

It says: no afterlife, no ordinary people or sages – all mere words. Although having attained empty stillness, they secretly practice lustful acts – though having realized some principles of emptiness, they secretly commit lust. Those receiving its lust likewise gain the empty mind, denying cause and effect: feeling no need to believe in the law of cause and effect anymore.

Sutra text: Thử danh nhật nguyệt, bạc thực tinh khí, kim ngọc chi thảo, lân phượng quy hạc. Kinh thiên vạn niên, bất tử vi linh, xuất sanh quốc độ, niên lão thành ma, não loạn thị nhân. Yếm túc tâm sanh, khứ bỉ nhân thể. Đệ tử dữ sư, đa hãm vương nạn.

Translation: This is called the essences of sun and moon in eclipse gathered into gold and jade, healing herbs, unicorns, phoenixes, turtles, cranes – passing thousands upon myriads of years undying, become spirits, born in this land, aged into demons, harassing this person. Sated, they arise and leave that person's body. Disciple and teacher mostly fall into legal peril.

Commentary: This is the essences gathered from solar and lunar eclipses into gold and jade, rare healing herbs, unicorns, phoenixes, turtles, cranes.

What kind of ghosts are these? Ghosts formed from essences of solar and lunar eclipses: when moon and sun meet in conjunction – called solar and lunar eclipse phenomena – streams of essence spread across the earth, gathering into gold and jade, a few kinds of rare healing herbs, unicorns, phoenixes, turtles, cranes. These essences keep those beings alive thousands upon myriads of years undying, at last become spirits, born in this land, aged into ghosts. They harass cultivators cultivating right samadhi. But at last, sated, no longer possessing people – ceasing to possess people. Teacher and disciple both fall into legal peril – prosecuted by law.

Sutra text: Nhữ đương tiên giác, bất nhập luân hồi. Mê hoặc bất tri, đọa vô gián ngục.

Translation: You should be awakened beforehand, and not enter the turning wheel. Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

Commentary: You should know this matter beforehand, lest you enter the demon king's turning wheel. Deluded and unknowing. Failing to awaken to this principle, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

10 – GREED FOR LONG LIFE

Sutra text: Hựu thiện nam tử, thọ ấm hư diệu, bất tao tà lự, viên định phát minh. Tam-ma-địa trung, tâm ái trường thọ, tân khổ nghiên cơ, tham cầu vĩnh diệt, khí phân đoạn sanh. Đốn hi biến dị, tế tướng thường trụ.

Translation: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed. Within samadhi the mind fond of long life – bitterly studying the subtle, greedily seeking immortality, discarding sectional birth-and-death, abruptly hoping the subtle transforming marks ever abide.

Commentary: Again that good man – the feeling skandha empty and wondrous, untroubled by deviant concerns, the perfect samadhi disclosed. In the empty, penetrating, wondrous state after the feeling skandha has dissolved.

Now the feeling skandha has become empty, penetrating, and wondrous; the cultivator cultivating right samadhi no longer has deviant concerns, dwelling in the bright, perfect samadhi. Within samadhi – perfect and wondrous – a sudden shift occurs. What? The mind fond of long life: suddenly the cultivator thinks: “How marvelous to live forever without dying!”

Hence bitterly studying the subtle, longing for immortality. Hence the cultivator bitterly, diligently studies the subtlest secret and wondrous methods, longing for immortality – wishing to stay forever young, never aging.

Discarding and renouncing sectional birth-and-death of the body.

Each character of “sectional birth-and-death” concerns the birth-and-death of each individual: each person has a portion, and each person a section. What does portion mean? You have a body, I have a body; you are a person, I am a person – you have your portion and I have my own portion. What is section? The lifespan – the span of time from living to dying. Section also means the body's stature, from head to foot.

Abruptly hoping for the subtle transforming birth-and-death.

Ordinary people must undergo sectional birth-and-death; those who have realized the four Arhat fruitions no longer pass through this state – but must still pass through “transformational birth-and-death” – thought after thought shifting: undergoing birth-and-death in every thought – changing in every thought, hence transformational: that is transformational birth-and-death. It concerns the mind-thoughts' unceasing continuity: thoughts continuous – this thought just arising, that thought at once perishing – like an endless stream. When the cultivator is no longer subject to sectional birth-and-death, suddenly he longs to attain transformational birth-and-death.

To ever abide long within those subtle marks – a very subtle, wondrous form: abiding in it forever means attaining eternal life.

Sutra text: Nhĩ thời thiên ma, hậu đắc kì tiện. Phi tinh phụ nhân khẩu thuyết kinh  pháp.

Translation: Then the heavenly demon gets its chance, sending its essence to possess another person, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma.

Commentary: The moment the cultivator cherishes the fantasy craving eternal life.

Then the heavenly demon gets its convenient chance, sending its essence flying to possess another person. The heavenly demon at once sends some of its followers to possess someone else, using that person's mouth to expound sutras and Dharma for the good man cultivating right samadhi to hear.

Sutra text: Kì nhân cánh bất giác tri ma trước, diệc ngôn tự đắc vô thượng niết-bàn. Lai bỉ cầu sanh thiện nam tử xứ, phu tòa thuyết pháp. Hảo ngôn tha phương, vãng hoàn vô trệ, hoặc kinh vạn lí, thuấn tức tái lai. Giai ư bỉ phương, thủ đắc kì vật. Hoặc ư nhất xứ, tại nhất trạch trung, xúc bộ chi gian, linh kì tòng đông, nghệ chí tây bích, thị nhân cấp hành, luy niên bất đáo. Nhân thử tâm tín, nghi Phật hiện tiền.

Translation: That person, even less aware of demonic possession, likewise claims to have attained unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the place of the good man seeking long life, it spreads its seat and preaches the Dharma – fond of boasting it can go anywhere and return unhindered, or traverse myriad miles, returning in an instant – all fetching objects from those places. Or in one place, within one house, within a few steps, making one go from east to west wall – that person walking swiftly, years never arriving. Hence the mind believes, suspecting a Buddha manifest.

Commentary: Since that person's mind is wholly controlled by the heavenly demon, he himself truly does not know he is demon-possessed, yet proclaims to have attained the wondrous fruition of unsurpassed nirvana. Coming to the good man seeking long life, spreading its seat, preaching the Dharma.

Fond of boasting it can go anywhere and return unhindered. What does the demon love to say? It says: “In a very brief moment I can go somewhere thousands upon myriads of miles away and return at once – I can go to Japan without a plane and buy goods back. If you do not believe, I shall demonstrate.”

It constantly displays spiritual powers for people to see – loves people seeing the inconceivable miracles it performs, saying: “I can come and go at will in the blink of an eye.”

It can roam a thousand miles and return in the blink of an eye, saying: “I can go and return within your single breath.”

It can fetch back objects from the places it has been.

Not only that – it can fetch back objects from the places it has been: buying goods back, asking: “Do you not believe me? Look at these goods – I bought them from company… in Japan – special sample goods, sold only to regular customers…” Then it produces for everyone a cassette player or radio made in Japan – no customs duty or import tax – truly manufactured by a Japanese company.

Or it can tell someone to walk from the east to the west side of a room within a distance of but a few steps (perhaps seven or eight paces) – yet though that person walk a whole year, never arriving: it cannot stretch the floor's space to a year's maximum. Seeing it perform so, hence everyone believes the possessed person's words, mistaking it for the Buddha.

They think: “Oh, a Buddha has come to lecture the Dharma for us.”

Sutra text: Khẩu trung thường thuyết, thập phương chúng sanh,  giai thị ngô tử. Ngã sanh chư Phật, ngã xuất thế giới, ngã thị nguyên Phật, xuất sanh tự nhiên, bất nhân tu đắc.

Translation: Its mouth constantly says: beings of the ten directions are all my children. I gave birth to the Buddhas; I brought forth the world. I am the original Buddha, born spontaneously of nature, not through cultivation.

Commentary: It constantly says: do you know? Beings of the ten directions are all my children; I gave birth to the Buddhas – shamelessly boasting it gave birth to the Buddhas.

I brought forth the world; I am the first Buddha – I am the earliest Buddha; no Buddha before me. I brought forth this world spontaneously, not through cultivation. I made this world spontaneously of nature, not through cultivation – and I was already a Buddha coming into this world: “I needed no cultivation to become a Buddha.”

Sutra text: Thử danh trụ thế tự tại thiên ma, sử kì quyến thuộc, như giá- văn-trà cập Tứ thiên vương, Tì xá đồng tử, vị phát tâm giả, lợi kì hư minh, thực bỉ tinh khí. Hoặc bất nhân sư, kì tu hành nhân, thân tự quan kiến, xưng chấp kim cương, dữ nhữ trường mệnh. Hiện mĩ nữ thân, thạnh hành tham dục. Vị du niên tuế, can não khô kiệt,  khẩu kiêm độc ngôn, thính nhược yêu  mị. Tiền nhân vị tường, đa hãm vương nạn. Vị cập  ngộ hình, tiên dĩ càn tử. Não loạn bỉ nhân, dĩ chí tồ vẫn.
