Translation: This is called the world-dwelling self-existent heavenly demon, sending such unawakened followers as chamunda ghosts and pishacha youths of the Four Heavenly Kings – exploiting his empty brightness to devour his essence and energy. Or, without a master, the cultivator himself sees them claiming to be vajra-holders granting long life. Manifesting beautiful women's bodies, ardently practicing greed and lust. Within less than a year, liver and brain dried up – the mouth muttering alone, sounding like goblins and sprites. Outsiders, not knowing the cause, mostly fall into legal peril. Before undergoing punishment, already dead and desiccated. Harassing the cultivator to death itself.

Commentary: This is called the world-dwelling self-existent heavenly demon, sending such unawakened followers as chamunda ghosts –

Chamunda (Skt. chamunda) means “pestilence-ghost: slave-ghost” – demons and ghosts working like slaves. It also means jealousy-ghost – ghosts forever jealous of every good thing others attain, always seeking to hinder people wanting to study the Buddhadharma: if someone wishes to become good, they drag him back toward evil. That is a kind of evil demon. The heavenly demon of the world-dwelling self-existent heaven sends such demons to harass the right-samadhi effort of cultivators – or sends pishacha youths from the Four Heavenly Kings' realm.

Pishacha ghosts especially love devouring essence and energy – devouring the essence and energy of plants and vegetation, and people's all the better. When men and women join in lustful acts, a kind of essence-energy is emitted, which they devour – a great many ghosts waiting nearby to devour this essence-energy: most perilous.

Exploiting his empty brightness, to devour the cultivator's essence and energy.

Exploiting that person's empty brightness, coming to devour the cultivator's essence and energy – these ghosts, unawakened (that is, dispatched by the heavenly demon) – like pishacha ghosts and others – love exploiting the cultivator's empty brightness: loving to devour the cultivator's essence and energy, yet the cultivator knows nothing of it.

Or, without a master (the possessed person), the cultivator himself sees them claiming to be vajra-holders granting long life.

Or, apart from any master (the possessed person), the cultivator sees someone claiming: “I am a vajra-holding spirit (Dharma protector), come to grant you long life – now I come to grant you long life; you shall live forever.”

Or they manifest beautiful women's bodies, ardently practicing greed and lust with the cultivator.

Or, having spoken, it turns into a beautiful woman, ardently practicing lust with the cultivator – both constantly doing so without rest.

Within less than a year, the cultivator's liver and brain dried up; the mouth muttering alone, sounding like goblins and sprites.

Within a year, vitality exhausted by such unbridled lust – vitality, essence, energy, spirit dried up within a year – through excess. The most important word is “ardently practicing.” The term is hard to convey in ordinary terms – but surely the woman says: “The more intoxicated in lust, the longer you live – soon attaining eternal life.” Craving boundless lifespan, he does not realize his life is being squeezed out, shortening minute by minute – within less than a year, life ends.

Muttering alone. Then its mouth mutters alone – in fact not talking to itself but talking with demons. Sounding like goblins and sprites: talking with demons, though people around see no demons.

I have met this kind of demon before: once I met a man visited by a woman every night – never visiting by day. But every evening she came, everyone in the apartment heard the clatter of her wooden clogs striking the wooden floor – hearing her walk, yet seeing no form. Whenever the woman came, he stripped off his clothes and crawled into bed – doing so regardless of people around. That is an example of this kind of demon.

Later an aged local spirit possessing a healing medium came to exorcise that female demon. That night, when the female demon came, it spoke with that spirit. The demon said: “Good! You wish to cure this man? Fine – from now on he shall recover. But from here, I shall come to you – we shall contest our magic together.”

Afterward it indeed went to that spirit, no longer visiting the man with whom it had done improper things morning to night.

I have told you many times: this kind of demon and ghost is most formidable.

Outsiders, not knowing the cause, mostly fall into legal peril. Before undergoing punishment, already dead and desiccated. Harassing the cultivator to death itself.

Outsiders cannot understand what happens – wholly unaware of this condition. In every case, such people fall into legal peril – the demon's acts arrested by law.

But before undergoing punishment – before being brought to trial – dead and desiccated: dying in prison, all essence, energy, and spirit dried up. The demon harasses and enchants the cultivator to death – destroying the cultivator's samadhi power until the person dies desiccated.

Sutra text: Nhữ đương tiên giác, bất nhập luân hồi. Mê hoặc bất tri, đọa vô gián ngục.

Translation: You should be awakened beforehand, and not enter the turning wheel. Deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell.

Commentary: Ananda, you should clearly know this condition – thoroughly understand this condition – lest you enter the turning wheel: recognizing these demonic states clearly, you will avoid the heavenly demon's trap – need not become the demon's household retinue – but deluded and unknowing, one falls into the uninterrupted hell – even the slightest blessing of human rebirth utterly lost.

THE WORLD-HONORED ONE'S CONCLUDING EXHORTATION ON THE THINKING SKANDHA

Sutra text: A-nan đương tri, thị thập chủng ma, ư mạt thế thời, tại ngã pháp trung, xuất gia tu đạo, hoặc phụ nhân thể, hoặc tự hiện hình. Giai ngôn dĩ thành chánh biến tri giác.

Translation: Ananda should know: in the Dharma-ending age these ten demons – either leaving home to cultivate within my Dharma, or possessing human bodies, or manifesting their own forms – all claim to have accomplished right and universal awakening.

Commentary: Ananda should know, especially in the Dharma-ending age, these ten demons appearing in the ten demonic states connected with the thinking skandha – either leaving home to cultivate within the Tathagata's Dharma, or possessing human bodies: the demon kings may possess other people's bodies, or manifesting their own various forms – displaying spiritual powers like demon kings, appearing in all kinds of shapes: Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, Arhats, or people of the heavens – demon kings can appear in any shape.

They all claim to have accomplished right and universal awakening: Right and Universal Knowledge is one of the Buddha's ten epithets – the Buddha is one complete with right knowledge and universal knowledge: right knowledge means knowing that the mind contains the myriad dharmas, and universal knowledge means knowing that the myriad dharmas are only mind. When people gain such truly right understanding, they become Buddhas – ones of Right and Universal Knowledge.

The heavenly demons fake themselves as Buddhas, falsely proclaiming to have attained Right and Universal Knowledge. When Shakyamuni Buddha was about to enter nirvana, he summoned the demon kings and taught: “From now on you must dwell within the moral code – do not violate it.”

The demon kings replied: “So you want us to practice by the code you made. Very well! In the Dharma-ending age I shall wear your robes, eat your food, then defecate into your alms bowl.”

Those words mean they will destroy the Dharma from within.

Hearing this, the Buddha said: “Then there is no way to save you – your conduct is too vicious and destructive.”

Hence the saying: “Worms in the lion's body eat the lion's flesh” – meaning in the Dharma-ending age demons are strong and the Dharma weak. So cultivators must be very careful. What are demon kings like? Usually quite unlike other people – with demonic aura within, showing some abnormal outer phenomena to prove they are demon kings.

Sutra text: Tán thán dâm dục, phá Phật luật nghi. Tiên ác ma sư, dữ ma đệ tử, dâm dâm tương truyền. Như thị tà tinh, mị kì tâm phủ, cận tắc cửu sanh, đa du bách thế. Linh chân tu hành, tổng vi ma quyến.

Translation: Praising lust, breaking the Buddha's moral code – former demonic teachers with demonic disciples, lustfully transmitting to one another. Such deviant essences enchanting their minds – near, at least nine lives; many, over a hundred generations – making true cultivators all become Mara's retinue.

Commentary: They praise lust.

How can we conclude someone is a demon? This: demons never praise the true method of cultivation – they praise lust and openly propagate lustful acts.

Breaking the Buddha's moral code.

It says: “The Buddha's precepts are utterly useless – do not keep them. Those precepts are only for Small Vehicle disciples to practice; we are Great Vehicle Bodhisattvas, needing to keep nothing!”

Demonic teachers, the demon king's disciples, transmitting lustful acts to one another: practicing lustful acts together and praising them, saying: “That is the most wondrous, wonderful Dharma-door – true emptiness and wondrous existence lie right therein.”

Such deviant essences – praising lust – enchanting cultivators' minds: since cultivators' minds, possessed and enchanted by deviant demons, immerse themselves in lust, openly praising it – doing all such things because demons have seized complete mastery of their minds.

Near, at least nine lives; many, over a hundred generations. Making true cultivators all become Mara's retinue.

At least nine lives: what does a life mean? The lifespan of a person, from birth to death? Not only that – more: about a hundred years. So nine lives are nine hundred years, and at most a hundred generations – a generation thirty years, a hundred generations three thousand years. True cultivators lost into the demon king's retinue at least nine lives (nine hundred years), at most a hundred generations (three thousand years).

Sutra text: Mệnh chung chi hậu, tất vi ma dân. Thất chánh biến tri, đọa vô gián ngục.

Translation: After life ends, they are sure to become Mara's subjects. Losing right and universal knowledge, they fall into the uninterrupted hell.

Commentary: After life ends: when the allotted span ends, at whatever point within the nine lives to a hundred generations, the cultivator dying, is sure to fall as one of Mara's subjects – unable to be a demon king, only a petty demon subject, an ordinary citizen among the demon folk.

Losing right and universal knowledge: losing right views, left only wrong knowledge and wrong views, carrying out whatever the demon king commands – and at last falling into the uninterrupted hell: after enjoying the demon's blessings to the end and the demon-subject's life ending, falling into the uninterrupted hell.

Sutra text: Nhữ kim vị tu, tiên thủ tịch diệt, túng đắc vô học. Lưu nguyện nhập bỉ mạt pháp chi trung, khởi đại từ bi, cứu độ chánh tâm thâm tín chúng sanh. Linh bất trước ma, đắc chánh tri kiến. Ngã kim độ nhữ dĩ xuất sanh tử. Nhữ tuân Phật ngữ, danh báo Phật ân.

Translation: Ananda, you should not yet hasten to still extinction – though you have attained beyond study. Keep your vow to enter that Dharma-ending age, giving rise to great compassion to save and deliver beings of right mind and deep faith, keeping them from demonic entanglement, gaining right views. I have now delivered you, already out of birth and death. Obeying the Buddha's words is called repaying the Buddha's kindness.

Commentary: Ananda, you should not yet hasten to enter nirvana – not entering nirvana early – but replacing the Tathagata, remaining in this Saha world to teach beings.

Although you have attained the beyond-study fruition. Keep your vow to enter that Dharma-ending age: though you have now attained the beyond-study fruition (at that time Ananda had realized the second Arhat fruition, not yet formally the beyond-study fruition; yet his path of effort toward realization was very bright, so he is regarded as having attained it).

The Buddha taught: you should keep the great-compassion vow – when the age of right Dharma has passed and the age of semblance Dharma is no more, the Dharma-ending age will come. Then give rise to great compassion to save and deliver beings of right mind and deep faith: Ananda, give rise to the great compassionate resolve to save all beings of true faith in the Dharma-ending age.

Keeping them from demonic entanglement: save and deliver beings, making them give rise to faith in you, lest they be deluded by the demon king, lest they follow the demon king, using the demon's means to harass beings anymore.

Helping them, beings of the Dharma-ending age, gain right views – meaning you and I and the beings right now, no one else. You should remind and awaken yourselves – you must have right views.

Shakyamuni Buddha further taught:

Ananda, the Tathagata has helped you out of birth and death: you have ended birth-and-death in the turning wheel, realized the second Arhat fruition, and known the path to the fourth fruition. So through your effort's result, it can be said you will transcend birth and death.

Obeying the Buddha's words now is called repaying the Buddha's kindness.

Now listen to the Buddha's words – practice what the Buddha taught and do not forget. By revering and obeying the Buddha's teaching, you can repay the Buddhas' profound kindness.

What does repaying the Buddha's kindness mean? If we revere and practice the Buddha's words, that is repaying the Buddha's kindness. To repay the Buddha's kindness, we must obey what the Buddha taught. Ananda, to repay the Buddha's kindness, must also follow the Buddha's teaching. We should obey Shakyamuni Buddha as well as the Dharma masters who taught us to study the sutras and principles. That is why from the start I ask you to faithfully follow the Buddha's words. I am not a Buddha, so I too obey the Buddha's teaching. In whatever we do, we should never forget the Buddha's words.

Sutra text: A-nan như thị, thập chủng thiền na hiện cảnh, giai thị tưởng ấm, dụng tâm giao hỗ, cố hiện tư sự.

Translation: Ananda, these ten states appearing in dhyana all come from the thinking skandha and the mind's applied effort interweaving, hence these occurrences.

Commentary: Ananda, the ten states explained – they only appear when the cultivator cultivates dhyana: striving with utmost effort, applying effort to reach the goal. Whence do these states appear? They occur all from the thinking skandha and the applying mind interweaving – formed by the contemplating mind's joint coordination.

These are transformations occurring while dissolving the thinking skandha, as the result of effort applied to the utmost. When you apply effort to the maximum, such states arise. But when they arise, do not foolishly mistake a thief for your son – do not be deluded by these states. When you sit in Chan, the effortful contemplating mind interweaves with the thinking skandha, forming a battlefield, as in warfare: if your samadhi power is stronger, the thinking skandha is conquered. But if the thinking skandha prevails and your samadhi effort weakens and scatters, the cultivator falls into demonic states and these ten states appear.

Sutra text: Chúng sanh ngoan mê, bất tự thốn lượng, phùng thử nhân duyên, mê bất tự thức, vị ngôn đăng thánh, đại vọng ngữ thành, đọa vô gián ngục.

Translation: Obstinate and deluded beings, not assessing themselves, encountering such conditions, deluded and unaware, claim to have ascended to sagehood – committing the great falsehood, they fall into the uninterrupted hell.

Commentary: Obstinate and deluded beings, not assessing their own measure – beings usually with attached minds: very stubborn, inflexible rather than yielding, foolish, lacking wisdom, unable to deliberate anything truly right by themselves.

Encountering such conditions, deluded and unaware: meeting such demonic states, lacking the clarity to assess. Most important: if you can assess the occurring state, demons cannot turn you. If you clearly recognize it, you will not be mistaken. Failing to recognize, you are deluded – delusion comes from unclear recognition. And what happens when the cultivator does not clearly understand this state?

Claiming to have realized sagehood: speaking such words as: “Do you know me? I have become a Buddha, and I shall tell you: for me becoming a Buddha was easier than a slab of bean curd.”

So very easy, is it not? Being easy, such people often say they have become Buddhas, realized the Way, awakened, investigated a meditation topic and understood those topics.

For instance, an American who came here today – a kind of “American Sixth Patriarch” who came some days ago: he does not bow to Buddhas, does not listen to Dharma – only eats lunch and leaves. The reason he leaves is demons dragging him away: with too much demonic aura in him, he feels ill at ease staying here even a minute past lunch. You should have a clear, general judgment of the demon-possessed: its style shows in thinking itself already a Buddha, hence no need to bow to Buddhas.

Committing the great falsehood, falling into the uninterrupted hell.

In the future, it is sure to fall into the uninterrupted hell – expect not a moment's respite: at least nine lives, at most a hundred generations. Not heeding the Buddhadharma because demonic power has seized it entirely: though wishing to listen, body and mind feel most uneasy, unable to sit still.

I have told you this story before – you should most attentively heed it. When you visit any monastery or Buddha-recitation hall, you must follow that Way-place's Chan rules: do as everyone does – do not stand while everyone bows to Buddhas. Those behaving so will never learn the Buddhadharma. Learning the Buddhadharma, you must be most humble, reverent, and sincere.

Sutra text: Nhữ đẳng tất tu, tương Như Lai ngữ, ư ngã diệt hậu, truyền thị mạt pháp, biến linh chúng sanh, khai ngộ tư nghĩa. Vô linh thiên ma đắc kì phương tiện. Bảo trì phúc hộ, thành vô thượng đạo.

Translation: In the Dharma-ending age, after the Tathagata's nirvana, you must all take the Tathagata's words and proclaim them to beings, awakening them to these meanings. Do not let the heavenly demons gain their advantage. Protect, shelter, and help beings accomplish the unsurpassed Way.

Commentary: In the Dharma-ending age, after the Tathagata's nirvana, you must all take the Tathagata's words and proclaim them to beings.

You all – Ananda, the great Bodhisattvas, great Bhikshus in the assembly, and great Elders: this is the Buddha's exhortation. “You must transmit the Tathagata's teaching continuously into the Dharma-ending age. Awakening them to these meanings: teaching them to understand the Shurangama Sutra; teaching them the Fifty Skandha-Demons – each demonic mark within the form, feeling, thinking, activity, and consciousness skandhas that I have explained to you. Wholeheartedly propagate this teaching for beings to understand.

Do not let the heavenly demons gain their advantage. If you let demons do whatever they please, you will be afflicted.

Protect and shelter – guarding the Buddhadharma – helping beings accomplish the unsurpassed Way.
